| [Zapier](#zapier) | sign in or token | high | Run actions in the apps connected to your Zapier account      |

## Details

### Cloudflare

`cloudflare`. The Cloudflare API: DNS, Workers, rules and more. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** high. Three tools (search, execute and docs) reach more than 2,500 endpoints, so turning tools on or off does not limit it. Only the scopes of the sign in or the permissions of the token do. It can change DNS, Workers and rules and create billable resources.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `user:read`, `account:read`.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, only for `mcp.cloudflare.com`. A Cloudflare API token, user or account. Scope it to the accounts and zones the agent should touch.

[Documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/mcp-servers-for-cloudflare/). Checked on 2026-11-14.

### Context7

`context7`. Up-to-date documentation and code examples for libraries. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** token.
* **Risk:** low. Reads public library documentation. The library name and the question the agent asks are sent to Context7's servers.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `CONTEXT7_API_KEY`, only for `mcp.context7.com`. A Context7 API key (starts with ctx7sk), made on the dashboard at context7.com. The server also answers without one, at much lower rate limits.

[Documentation](https://context7.com/docs/resources/all-clients). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Datadog

`datadog`. Search logs, metrics, traces, monitors and dashboards in Datadog. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** medium. Reads logs, metrics, traces and other observability data, and some tools can change things such as dashboards, notebooks and monitors in the person's organization. Access follows the person's Datadog permissions.
* **Address:** `https://{site}/v1/mcp` (the host is one of 7, see the option below)
* **Sign in:** OAuth.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `DATADOG_MCP_TOKEN`, only for `mcp.datadoghq.com`, `mcp.us3.datadoghq.com`, `mcp.us5.datadoghq.com`, `mcp.datadoghq.eu`, `mcp.ap1.datadoghq.com`, `mcp.ap2.datadoghq.com`, `mcp.uk1.datadoghq.com`. A Personal Access Token or Service Access Token made in Datadog. It is sent as a bearer token.

| Option |                                                                                                                                                                   What it does                                                                                                                                                                   |   Goes to   |     For      |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|--------------|
| `site` | The MCP address for the site where your Datadog organization is hosted. Check the address you use to sign in to Datadog. One of: `mcp.datadoghq.com` (US1), `mcp.us3.datadoghq.com` (US3), `mcp.us5.datadoghq.com` (US5), `mcp.datadoghq.eu` (EU1), `mcp.ap1.datadoghq.com` (AP1), `mcp.ap2.datadoghq.com` (AP2), `mcp.uk1.datadoghq.com` (UK1). | host `site` | every way in |

[Documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/mcp_server/setup/). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Excalidraw

`excalidraw`. Draw hand-drawn style diagrams and sketches. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** no sign in.
* **Risk:** low. A public server run by a third party with no account. Whatever the agent sends to draw a diagram goes to that server. It does not reach the person's own data.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.excalidraw.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** none. A person switches it on for themselves, and no secret is stored.

[Documentation](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw-mcp). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Git

`git`. Read, search and change local Git repositories. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** a local program (an admin).
* **Risk:** medium. Can add, reset, commit, merge and switch branches. Described by its authors as in early development. Without a repository set it can reach every repository the process can.
* **Runs:** `uvx mcp-server-git==2026.11.11` on the machine the agent runs on. It needs `uvx` on the PATH. Install uv (<https://docs.astral.sh/uv/>) so the agent can start this server. It runs on the machine the agent runs on, in the folder you start the agent from.
* **Sign in:** none. A person switches it on for themselves, and no secret is stored.

|    Option    |                                                                       What it does                                                                       |      Goes to       |     For      |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|--------------|
| `repository` | A path inside a Git working tree. The server then works only in that repository. Left empty, it can read and write any repository the process can reach. | arg `--repository` | every way in |

[Documentation](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/src/git). Checked on 2026-11-17.

### GitHub

`github`. Repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions and code search. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** token.
* **Risk:** high. Can create pull requests, push files, merge, delete files and trigger Actions. Prefer a fine-grained token with read access first.
* **Address:** `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, only for `api.githubcopilot.com`. A personal access token. Give it only the repositories and permissions the agent needs.

|   Option   |                                                               What it does                                                               |         Goes to         |     For      |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|--------------|
| `toolsets` | A comma separated list of the GitHub toolsets to enable, for example issues,pull_requests. Left empty, the server's default set is used. | header `X-MCP-Toolsets` | every way in |
| `readonly` | Turns off every tool that changes something.                                                                                             | header `X-MCP-Readonly` | every way in |

[Documentation](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server). Checked on 2026-11-14.

### Netlify

`netlify`. Create, deploy and manage Netlify sites from an agent. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** high. Can create and change sites and publish deploys in the person's Netlify account, which can reach production sites. Start with a test site.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.netlify.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.

[Documentation](https://docs.netlify.com/build/build-with-ai/netlify-mcp-server/). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Supabase

`supabase`. Database, SQL, migrations, projects and branches. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** high. Runs SQL and migrations and can create paid projects. Read only is on by default; add a project to limit it to one. Table data can carry prompt injection, so never give it to end users.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, only for `mcp.supabase.com`. A personal access token.

|    Option     |                                              What it does                                              |       Goes to       |     For      |
|---------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|--------------|
| `project_ref` | Limits the connector to one project and turns off the account tools.                                   | query `project_ref` | every way in |
| `read_only`   | Runs queries as a read only Postgres user. On by default.                                              | query `read_only`   | every way in |
| `features`    | A comma separated list of the tool groups to enable. Left empty, the server's default groups are used. | query `features`    | every way in |

[Documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/mcp). Checked on 2026-11-14.

### Vercel

`vercel`. Search Vercel docs, manage projects, inspect deployments and logs, and query Web Analytics. Listed under Developer.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** high. Can manage projects and deployments in the person's Vercel account, which can reach production sites. Start with a test team or project.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.vercel.com`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.

[Documentation](https://vercel.com/docs/mcp/vercel-mcp). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Asana

`asana`. Search, read, create and update tasks, projects and comments in Asana. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in (your own app).
* **Risk:** medium. Can create and change tasks, projects and comments in the workspaces the person can reach.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`
* **Sign in, with your own app:** the service takes no dynamic client registration, so an admin registers an app and sets `ASANA_CLIENT_ID` and `ASANA_CLIENT_SECRET` in the agent's vault or environment. In the Asana developer console create a new app of type MCP app, add the redirect address (the public address of this app followed by /__bxagents/connect/callback) on its OAuth page, and under Manage distribution allow the workspaces that will use it. Asana does not accept dynamic client registration. Scopes: `default`.

[Documentation](https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Atlassian (Jira and Confluence)

`atlassian`. Jira work items, Confluence pages, Bitbucket. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** medium. Creates and updates work items and pages and posts comments.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN`, only for `mcp.atlassian.com`. A service account API key, sent as a Bearer token. An organization admin must allow API token sign in first. Personal API tokens use Basic authentication and are not supported here. Tokens are not tied to one site and some tools are missing.

[Documentation](https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server/docs/getting-started-with-the-atlassian-remote-mcp-server/). Checked on 2026-11-14.

### Box

`box`. Search and read files and folders, ask Box AI, create folders and comments. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in (your own app).
* **Risk:** medium. Can create folders, comments and new file versions, and some tools can change file properties or create shared links. Tools that write are off by default in Box. People can only reach content they already have access to.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.box.com`
* **Sign in, with your own app:** the service takes no dynamic client registration, so an admin registers an app and sets `BOX_CLIENT_ID` and `BOX_CLIENT_SECRET` in the agent's vault or environment. A Box admin opens Integrations in the Admin Console, configures the Box MCP server, adds Integration Credentials, copies the client id and secret, enters the redirect address (the public address of this app followed by /__bxagents/connect/callback) and selects the access scopes. Box also lists docgen.readwrite, which needs an Enterprise Advanced license. Scopes: `root_readwrite`, `ai.readwrite`.

[Documentation](https://developer.box.com/guides/box-mcp/remote/). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Calendly

`calendly`. List event types and meetings, create scheduling links and bookings, read meeting notes. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** high. Can book and cancel meetings, create event types, mark no-shows and invite people to the organization, which can send emails to other people.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.calendly.com`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `mcp:scheduling:read`, `mcp:scheduling:write`.

[Documentation](https://developer.calendly.com/docs/mcp/calendly-mcp-server). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Canva

`canva`. Create, find, edit, comment on and export Canva designs and assets. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in (your own app).
* **Risk:** medium. Can create and edit designs, upload assets, add comments and move items between folders in the person's own Canva account.
* **Address:** `https://api.canva.com/connect/v1/mcp`
* **Sign in, with your own app:** the service takes no dynamic client registration, so an admin registers an app and sets `CANVA_CLIENT_ID` and `CANVA_CLIENT_SECRET` in the agent's vault or environment. In the Canva Developer Portal create an app, open Outside Canva, turn on Canva MCP under Integration methods, copy the client id, generate a client secret, and add the redirect address (the public address of this app followed by /__bxagents/connect/callback) under Redirect URLs. Each person signs in with their own Canva account. Scopes: `profile:read`, `design:meta:read`, `design:content:read`, `design:content:write`, `folder:read`, `folder:write`, `brandtemplate:meta:read`, `brandtemplate:content:read`, `brandtemplate:content:write`, `comment:read`, `comment:write`, `asset:read`, `asset:write`, `brandkit:read`, `help:answers:read`, `help:answers:write`.

[Documentation](https://www.canva.dev/blog/developers/canva-mcp-ga/). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### ClickUp

`clickup`. Search, create and update tasks, documents and chat messages. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** high. Can create and change tasks and documents and post chat messages that other people in the workspace see. It has no delete tools.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.

[Documentation](https://developer.clickup.com/docs/connect-an-ai-assistant-to-clickups-mcp-server). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Gamma

`gamma`. Create, search, edit and export presentations, documents and webpages. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** medium. Can create and edit gammas in the workspace and uses the workspace's credits when it generates or edits.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.gamma.app/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.

[Documentation](https://developers.gamma.app/mcp/gamma-mcp-server). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### HyperFrames by HeyGen

`hyperframes`. Create, revise and render videos from a text description. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** medium. Creates and renders videos in the person's HeyGen account, which can use credits. The documentation calls this connector a beta.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.heygen.com/mcp/hyperframes/`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.

[Documentation](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/mcp). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Linear

`linear`. Find, create and update issues, projects, documents and comments. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** medium. Can create and change issues, projects, documents and comments in the workspace. Use a read-only key to limit it.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `read`, `write`.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `LINEAR_API_KEY`, only for `mcp.linear.app`. A Linear API key, or an OAuth access token from your own Linear OAuth app. A key with only the Read permission gives read-only access.

[Documentation](https://linear.app/docs/mcp). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Notion

`notion`. Search, read, create and update pages and databases. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** medium. Can edit and delete pages and databases.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `NOTION_MCP_TOKEN`, only for `mcp.notion.com`. A token made by a workspace owner under New MCP token in the developer portal. Business and Enterprise plans only.

[Documentation](https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/get-started-with-mcp). Checked on 2026-11-14.

### RingCentral Chat

`ringcentral-chat`. Team messaging chats, direct conversations, teams and posts in RingEX. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** high. Can read and post messages in your chats and teams as you. This is a RingCentral Labs preview.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com/ringex/team-chat`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `ReadAccounts`, `TeamMessaging`.

[Documentation](https://developers.ringcentral.com/mcp/servers/). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### RingCentral Phone

`ringcentral-phone`. Call logs, contacts, messages, presence and SMS in RingEX. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** high. Can read call history and messages and send SMS from your number. This is a RingCentral Labs preview.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com/ringex/phone`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `ReadAccounts`, `ReadContacts`, `ReadCallLog`, `AI`, `ReadMessages`, `ReadPresence`, `SMS`.

[Documentation](https://developers.ringcentral.com/mcp/servers/). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Slack

`slack`. Search channels and people, read threads, send messages, canvases, files and lists. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in (your own app) or token.
* **Risk:** high. Can send and schedule messages as the person, add reactions, create channels and canvases, upload files and read private channels and direct messages the token reaches. Use a test workspace first, and give the token read scopes only to start with.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`
* **Sign in, with your own app:** the service takes no dynamic client registration, so an admin registers an app and sets `SLACK_CLIENT_ID` and `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET` in the agent's vault or environment. Register a Slack app at api.slack.com/apps that is internal to your workspace or published in the Slack Marketplace (Slack refuses MCP for other apps, and does not accept dynamic client registration). Add the user scopes listed, and add the app public address followed by /__bxagents/connect/callback as a redirect URL. Scopes: `search:read.public`, `search:read.private`, `search:read.mpim`, `search:read.im`, `search:read.files`, `search:read.users`, `files:read`, `files:write`, `emoji:read`, `chat:write`, `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `mpim:history`, `im:history`, `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`, `channels:write`, `groups:write`, `im:write`, `mpim:write`, `reactions:read`, `reactions:write`, `canvases:read`, `canvases:write`, `users:read`, `users:read.email`, `lists:read`, `lists:write`.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `SLACK_MCP_TOKEN`, only for `mcp.slack.com`. A Slack user token (xoxp-...) of a Slack app that is internal to your workspace or published in the Slack Marketplace, with only the scopes the agent needs (docs.slack.dev lists the scopes of each tool). Slack does not accept dynamic client registration, so there is no sign in, and an app that is neither internal nor published is refused. (not verified yet)

[Documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Whop

`whop`. Search the Whop docs and read or change live Whop data. Listed under Productivity.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** high. Asks for admin access and works on production data only. It can change products, plans and payments data. There is no sandbox.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.whop.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `admin`.

[Documentation](https://docs.whop.com/developer/guides/ai_and_mcp.md). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### HubSpot

`hubspot`. Search and update CRM records, activities, content and campaigns in HubSpot. Listed under Sales.

* **Connects with:** sign in (your own app).
* **Risk:** high. Can create and change CRM records, publish landing pages and blog posts, and create or schedule social posts. Use read access only to start with.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.hubspot.com`
* **Sign in, with your own app:** the service takes no dynamic client registration, so an admin registers an app and sets `HUBSPOT_CLIENT_ID` and `HUBSPOT_CLIENT_SECRET` in the agent's vault or environment. In HubSpot go to Development, then MCP Connectors, and create an MCP connector with the redirect address (the public address of this app followed by /__bxagents/connect/callback). Copy its client id and client secret. The account must be on the HubSpot developer platform, and an admin connects first. Scopes come from what the person grants at install.

[Documentation](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/developer-platform/build-apps/integrate-with-the-remote-hubspot-mcp-server). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Meltwater

`meltwater`. Media and social mentions, saved searches and insights from Meltwater. Listed under Sales.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** low. Reads your saved searches, tags and media and social data. Which tools you get depends on your Meltwater package.
* **Address:** `https://api.meltwater.com/v2/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `tools:read`, `tools:call`.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `MELTWATER_API_KEY`, only for `api.meltwater.com`. It is sent in the `apikey` header. Make an API token in the Meltwater app (see API Credentials in the Meltwater developer portal) and paste it here. Your plan must include Meltwater MCP.

[Documentation](https://developer.meltwater.com/guides/meltwater-mcp/connectors/custom/). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Bigdata.com

`bigdata`. Search financial news, filings, earnings transcripts and analyst research. Listed under Finance.

* **Connects with:** token.
* **Risk:** low. Reads financial documents and market data. It cannot change anything. You need a Bigdata.com account.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.bigdata.com/`
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `BIGDATA_API_KEY`, only for `mcp.bigdata.com`. It is sent in the `x-api-key` header. Make an API key in the Bigdata.com Developer Platform under API Keys (platform.bigdata.com/api-keys) and paste it here.

[Documentation](https://docs.bigdata.com/mcp-reference/api-integrations/mcp-api-integration.md). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Daloopa

`daloopa`. Company financials, KPIs, filings and earnings transcripts. Listed under Finance.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** low. Reads financial data, filings and stock prices. It cannot change anything. You need a Daloopa account.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.daloopa.com/server/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `DALOOPA_API_KEY`, only for `mcp.daloopa.com`. It is sent in the `X-API-KEY` header. Use your Daloopa API key. Daloopa sales or support gives you one. The key is sent as is, with no token step.

[Documentation](https://docs.daloopa.com/docs/mcp-authentication.md). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### S\&P Global

`spglobal`. Financial data and company research from the Kensho LLM-ready API. Listed under Finance.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** low. Reads financial and market data. It cannot change anything. You need a Kensho account.
* **Address:** `https://kfinance.kensho.com/integrations/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `kensho:app:kfinance`, `offline_access`.

[Documentation](https://docs.kensho.com/llmreadyapi/mcp). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Stripe

`stripe`. Customers, invoices, subscriptions, refunds and documentation search. Listed under Finance.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** high. Moves money. Its write tool covers POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE. Stripe asks for human confirmation on refunds and outbound payments.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.stripe.com`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `mcp`.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `STRIPE_AGENT_API_KEY`, only for `mcp.stripe.com`. An agent API key with the smallest set of permissions. Use a sandbox account first. Stripe stops accepting full-access secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag on 2026-11-30.

|       Option       |                                                        What it does                                                        |         Goes to         |   For   |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------|
| `connectedAccount` | The id of a connected account (acct_...) to act as. Platform agent API keys only; OAuth cannot act as a connected account. | header `Stripe-Account` | a token |

[Documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/mcp). Checked on 2026-11-14.

### Mixpanel

`mixpanel`. Run reports on events, funnels and retention, and browse dashboards. Listed under Analytics.

* **Connects with:** sign in.
* **Risk:** medium. Reads analytics data, and can also create, edit and delete dashboards, tags and event definitions in the person's project. The admin picks the region that matches the project.
* **Address:** `https://{region}/mcp` (the host is one of 3, see the option below)
* **Sign in:** OAuth.

|  Option  |                                                                    What it does                                                                     |    Goes to    |     For      |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|--------------|
| `region` | The region where your Mixpanel project stores its data. One of: `mcp.mixpanel.com` (US), `mcp-eu.mixpanel.com` (EU), `mcp-in.mixpanel.com` (India). | host `region` | every way in |

[Documentation](https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/mcp). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Buffer

`buffer`. Read channels and queue, schedule and edit posts, capture ideas and pull post analytics. Listed under Social Media.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** high. Can schedule, edit and delete posts that go out to the connected social channels. Use a test channel first.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.buffer.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `BUFFER_API_KEY`, only for `mcp.buffer.com`. A Buffer API key made in Settings, API at publish.buffer.com/settings/api. It reaches every organization and channel in the account.

[Documentation](https://developers.buffer.com/guides/integrations/mcp.md). Checked on 2026-11-26.

### Metricool

`metricool`. Manage brands, read social analytics and schedule posts. Listed under Social Media.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** high. Can schedule and publish posts to the connected social accounts and change brand settings. Plan limits still apply.
* **Address:** `https://ai.metricool.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `mcp:read`, `mcp:write`.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `METRICOOL_API_KEY`, only for `ai.metricool.com`. It is sent in the `X-Mc-Auth` header. Copy your Metricool API key from Account Settings, then API (app.metricool.com/user-settings/api) and paste it here.

[Documentation](https://help.metricool.com/how-to-connect-metricools-mcp-with-claude-0l84v.md). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### X Ads

`x-ads`. Read X Ads accounts and analytics, and create and manage campaigns. Listed under Advertising.

* **Connects with:** sign in (your own app).
* **Risk:** high. Can create and change campaigns, line items, audiences and creatives, and activate campaigns that spend money. New campaigns start paused.
* **Address:** `https://ads-api.x.com/mcp`
* **Sign in, with your own app:** the service takes no dynamic client registration, so an admin registers an app and sets `X_ADS_CLIENT_ID` (a public client has no secret) in the agent's vault or environment. In the X Developer Console create or reuse an app with Read and Write permission, type Native App (public client, PKCE, no secret), and add the redirect address (the public address of this app followed by /__bxagents/connect/callback). Enable Ads API access under Project Access, and copy the OAuth 2.0 client id. Scopes: `ads.read`, `ads.write`, `offline.access`.

[Documentation](https://docs.x.com/x-ads-api/mcp). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Wix

`wix`. Search Wix documentation and make API calls on your Wix sites. Listed under Apps.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** high. Can change site content, store data and other settings through the Wix APIs, including on a live site.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.wix.com/mcp`
* **Sign in:** OAuth with the scopes `offline_access`.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `WIX_API_KEY`, only for `mcp.wix.com`. It is sent alone in the `Authorization` header. Make an API key in your Wix account (API Keys page in the Wix developer docs) and paste it here. The key is sent alone, without Bearer. Also fill in your Wix account ID below.

|      Option      |                    What it does                     |         Goes to         |   For   |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------|
| `wix_account_id` | The ID of your Wix account. Needed with an API key. | header `wix-account-id` | a token |

[Documentation](https://dev.wix.com/docs/sdk/articles/use-the-wix-mcp/about-the-wix-mcp.md). Checked on 2026-11-27.

### Zapier

`zapier`. Run actions in the apps connected to your Zapier account. Listed under Apps.

* **Connects with:** sign in or token.
* **Risk:** high. Can run any action you enable in Zapier, such as sending email and messages or changing records in other apps. Enable only the actions you need.
* **Address:** `https://mcp.zapier.com/api/v1/connect`
* **Sign in:** OAuth.
* **Token:** sealed in the vault as `ZAPIER_MCP_TOKEN`, only for `mcp.zapier.com`. A connection token. Create a server at mcp.zapier.com, then generate its token. It is shown once and stays valid until you regenerate it.

[Documentation](https://docs.zapier.com/mcp/overview/how-connections-work.md). Checked on 2026-11-26.

markdown:
# Connectors

A **connector** is a ready-made connection to a service that has an MCP server. BX Agents ships with 35, in groups (Developer, Productivity, Sales, Finance, Analytics, Microsoft 365, Social Media, Advertising and Apps): [the connector catalog](/next/conventions/connector-catalog/index.html) lists each one. Every agent offers them by default. Offering one does not connect it: nothing contacts a service until a person connects their own account.

* **Personal.** A token or sign in belongs to one person. The agent uses it only when that person asks, and two people never share a token or a session.
* **Sealed.** Tokens are stored in the [vault](/next/conventions/vault/index.html), locked to the host of the service. The model never sees one.
* **Your own servers still work.** The services you write under `mcpServers` in [Agent.yml](/next/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html) are separate. An `mcpServers` entry with the same name as a connector replaces that connector, and the build warns.

![The Connectors page: the built-in connectors, each with its risk and how it signs in](/next/assets/webui/connectors.png)

## States

|      State      |                                                              Meaning                                                              |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| available       | Offered, not connected by you                                                                                                     |
| connected       | Connected, its tools are on                                                                                                       |
| needs attention | Connected, but the service refused the token (it failed, expired or was revoked), at connect time or during a call. Connect again |
| needs a program | A local program the connector runs (such as `uvx` for Git) is not installed                                                       |

## Limit them in Agent.yml

```yaml
# Agent.yml
connectors:                  # leave the key out to offer every connector
  only: [ github, notion ]   # just these
  override:
    github:
      timeout: 30000
      options: { readonly: true }
      tools: [ search_repositories ]
  toolWarning: 100           # warn a person above this many tools
```

Or offer everything except some:

```yaml
connectors:
  exclude: [ stripe ]
```

`exclude` names connectors that `only` would offer, so using both for different connectors is an error at build.

`connectors: none` turns the catalog off. The order of evaluation is `only`, then `exclude`, then `override`. `override` accepts `timeout` (milliseconds, 1000 to 600000), `options` (the values a connector asks for), `scopes` (only for connectors with a sign in) and `tools` (the most a person may switch on: a ceiling, not a default). `toolWarning` is a whole number from 10 to 2000 (100 by default). Everything is checked when the project is built, and `bxAgents inspect` shows what each agent offers.

## Connecting

A connector asks for either a token or a sign in, shown on its page in the [catalog](/next/conventions/connector-catalog/index.html).

|        Where         |                                                                                                                     How                                                                                                                     |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Web page             | The **Connectors** page, with tabs for All, Connected, Needs attention and In Agent.yml, each at its own address (`<path>/connectors/all`, `connected`, `attention`, `agent`). See [web-ui](/next/conventions/web-ui/index.html#connectors) |
| Chat in the terminal | `/connect`, `/connect NAME`, `/connect NAME off`, `/connect NAME tools`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| CLI                  | `bxAgents connect`, `bxAgents connect NAME`                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Gateways             | `/connect` lists them. A token is never typed in a chat: the reply points to the web page                                                                                                                                                   |

Medium and high risk connectors show what they can do and ask for confirmation first. A token is checked with the service before it is sealed. At the terminal the token goes in a hidden box. For scripts:

```bash
bxAgents connect github --token-env=GITHUB_TOKEN --confirm
printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | bxAgents connect github --stdin --confirm
bxAgents connect github tools off delete_file    # also: tools on NAME, tools off all, tools readonly
bxAgents connect github options repository=/path/to/repo   # connectors with options
```

In chat, `--token-env` is honored only on the terminal (`tui`) transport. A token connected on the web belongs to that web account, not to the same person's chat identity on a platform. Programs the agent runs on its own machine (Git) are connected by an admin when the agent is served. Switching it off stops the process, and changing an option restarts it with the new value, at once.

## Tools and the tool count

Each person can turn tools on and off, one by one, from the drawer on the web page or with `tools` in the terminal. Tools are listed alphabetically. When the total on exceeds `toolWarning`, the page warns that the model may choose worse. An admin's `tools` override sets the ceiling for everyone. A tool that is off, over the ceiling or not connected is refused when the model calls it, not only hidden from it.

## Scheduled runs

A [routine](/next/conventions/routines/index.html) runs as the person who made it, so it uses that person's connectors. A `schedules/*.bx` file belongs to no person and gets no connector tools.

## API

|              Route              |                                  Does                                   |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `GET /connectors`               | The connectors, your state for each, and your tool count. Never a token |
| `POST /connectors/connect`      | Connect one (token, sign in, or local program)                          |
| `POST /connectors/disconnect`   | Disconnect one                                                          |
| `POST /connectors/options`      | Change a connector's options                                            |
| `GET`, `POST /connectors/tools` | List and switch tools                                                   |

## Ways a connector can ask you in

Most connectors take a sign in or a token. A few need something else, and the catalog files say so:

* **A token in another header.** A token method may name its `header` and `prefix`: `header: x-api-key` with `prefix: ""` sends the key alone in that header, `Authorization` with `prefix: ""` sends it without `Bearer`. The default is `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A header that belongs to the connection (Host, Cookie, Content-Type and a few more) is refused when the file is checked. The token is still sealed in the vault and sent only to the connector's host.
* **A host chosen from a list.** The address may be `https://{site}/mcp`, with one option of `target: host` that lists the hosts it may be (`choices`, each a host name and a label) and a default. A value that is not on the list is never used, at connect time or when the connector is called, so nobody can point a connector at a server of their own. A token is sealed for every host on the list. A connector with a sign in uses the host the admin sets in `connectors.override`; one with a token lets each person choose.
* **A public server.** `auth: [ { type: none } ]` on a web connector means it asks for nothing. A person switches it on for themselves, no secret is stored, and the entry's risk note says that what the agent sends goes to a third party.
* **A sign in through an app of your own.** Some services do not allow dynamic client registration, so no sign in can be made for them out of the box. Their files have `app: own` on the oauth method. Until an admin has set the app, the connector says so, with how to register it, and nobody can connect it. The admin registers an app with the service, gives it the redirect address (the app's public address followed by `<api path>/connect/callback`, `/__bxagents/connect/callback` by default) and sets the client id, and the client secret when the service gives one, under the names the file lists (`SLACK_CLIENT_ID` and `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET` for Slack) as secrets of the agent in the vault or as environment variables, then restarts the agent. They are read when the agent starts and held in memory: never written to a file, never returned by the API.

## Adding a connector

The catalog is the YAML files in `src/main/bx/catalog/connectors/`. Add one file, run `bxAgents connectors check`, then regenerate the [catalog page](/next/conventions/connector-catalog/index.html) with `tools/generate-connector-docs.bxs`. A spec fails if the page is stale. Every entry records the date it was checked against the service's own documentation (`verifiedOn`).

## Needs bx-ai 3.8

Signing in to a served agent needs the bx-ai fix for web requests (argument `form` reserved in web requests, bx-ai issue 334). Tokens connected by hand are not affected.

# Data and volumes

An agent keeps its state in one place, the **data home** , and reaches the rest of your machine only through **volumes** : folders you name in `Agent.yml`. `bxAgents data` shows both, and `bxAgents backup` and `restore` keep the data safe.

## The data home

```text
<data home>/
  README.md      what this folder is, written once
  chat.db        conversations and the agents' memory of them, notes, access tokens, secrets and usage counts
  files/         what the agent writes (the `files` volume)
  skills/        skills the agent saves
  routines/      reports saved by routines, one folder each (see routines)
  logs/          what the agent logs, one file per area (see logs)
  backups/       written by bxAgents backup
  Agent.yml      your own settings for this agent on this machine: how the chat looks and any other setting (see layered settings), made when you first save one
```

There is always a home. Where it is, first match wins:

1. The environment variable `BXAGENTS_HOME`.
2. `data.home` in `Agent.yml`.
3. The folder of `BXAGENTS_DB` when that names a file called `chat.db` (what `serve` and `chat` set).
4. `data/` in the project, when it already holds a `chat.db`. A project from before this convention keeps its data.
5. **`~/.bxagents/<agent name>`**, the convention. It is outside the project and outside the build, so a new build never replaces it, and it is the same place in development and when deployed.
6. `data/` in the project, only for an agent that has no name.

```yaml
# Agent.yml
name: nanobox
data:
  home: ~/.nanobox      # an absolute path, one starting with ~, or one relative to the project
```

`BXAGENTS_DB` keeps working and names the database file on its own.

The agent name is turned into a safe folder name: letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, the rest become a dash. Two projects with the same agent name share one home, so give them different names, or set `data.home` on one.

The folders and the README are made the first time the app or `chat` starts. Nothing is made just by asking where the home is.

## Volumes

A volume is a folder on this machine that the agent's file tools may use, under a name.

```yaml
# Agent.yml
volumes:
  notes:
    path: ~/Notes
    mode: rw                 # rw (read and write) or ro (read only, the default)
    description: My notes    # optional, up to 200 characters
  downloads:
    path: ~/Downloads
```

Every agent also has `files`: the `files/` folder of its data home, always read and write.

|   Rule   |                                             Detail                                             |
|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Names    | Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 1 to 32 characters. `files` is taken. At most 32 volumes |
| `path`   | Absolute, starting with `~`, or relative to the project. It must exist when the app starts     |
| Too wide | The whole disk or the whole home folder is refused. So is the data home itself                 |
| Keys     | `path`, `mode`, `description`. Anything else is refused                                        |
| When     | Volumes are fixed when the app starts. The agent cannot add one, and neither can an API        |

An agent that lists bx-ai's file tools (`readFile@bxai`, `writeFile@bxai`, and so on) gets the project's volumes with no further setting. An agent that sets `toolOptions.bxai.allowedPaths` itself keeps those full paths instead, and cannot also use volumes.

### How the agent sees them

The agent writes a path as `volume:path`, for example `notes:todo.md`. A path with no volume is in `files`.

* A full path on the machine is refused, and so is anything that climbs out of its volume with `..` or a symbolic link.
* A read only volume can be read, listed and copied from, but not written to, moved, or deleted from.
* Results and error messages name volumes. The agent never sees where a volume is on the machine.
* `listAllowedDirectories` answers with the volumes, their modes and their descriptions.

### Seeing them

* **In chat:** `/volumes` lists the volumes by name, mode and description, in the terminal, the web page and gateways. It never shows a folder on the machine.
* **Over the API:** `GET /volumes` answers the same list to anyone who may call the API. `GET /data` answers the data home, the size of each part and the folder of each volume, and is for admins only, since it shows paths.
* **In `doctor`:** it reports the data home, where it came from, and whether it can be written. It makes nothing.

![The Data and backups page: where the agent keeps everything, the volumes, and the backups](/next/assets/webui/webui-data.png)

The web app shows all of this on its [Data and backups page](/next/conventions/web-ui/index.html#data-and-backups) (admins only).

## Skills the agent saves

A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md`: instructions the agent loads by name when a task calls for them. There are three levels:

|        Level         |                           Where                           |                                      Written by                                      |  `origin`   |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| Installed            | `.agents/skills/` in the project                          | The registry tools (`npx skills`, `bxAgents skills install`), restored at build time | `installed` |
| Ships with the agent | `skills/` in the project, and the skills extensions carry | You                                                                                  | `project`   |
| The agent's own      | `skills/` in the data home                                | The agent, with its `skill_save` tool                                                | `agent`     |
| bxAgents' own        | `skills/` inside the bxAgents module                      | bxAgents                                                                             | `bxagents`  |

The build copies the first two into the app, and the app loads the third at start and the moment a skill is saved. A diagram of the levels is on the [skills page](/next/conventions/skills/index.html#the-three-levels). A skill that ships with the agent wins over an installed one of the same name.

After a task that took real steps and is likely to come up again, the root agent can call `skill_save( name, description, content )`. The skill is written to the data home and is in the agent's skill list at once, with no restart. Subagents are given the skills when they are built; they cannot save any.

* **The first two levels win.** The agent cannot take the name of an installed skill or one that ships with the agent, or replace it. It can save over a skill it wrote itself, to improve it.
* **Approval.** Each save is approved by a person, as for any tool that needs approval, unless `skills.autoApprove: true`.
* **Limits.** A name is a folder name (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`). A description is up to 500 characters and the content up to 20,000. The agent keeps up to 50 skills; saving over one it has is always allowed.
* **Off switch.** `skills.agentCanSave: false` takes the tool away.

```yaml
skills:
  agentCanSave: true     # default true; the root agent only
  autoApprove: false     # default false
```

A saved skill is part of the data home, so `backup` and `restore` carry it. To remove one, delete its folder.

### Seeing the skills

* **In chat:** `/skills` lists every skill with its level: installed, project, bxagents or agent.
* **Over the API:** `GET /skills` answers `{ skills: [ { name, description, origin } ] }` (`origin` is `installed`, `project`, `bxagents` or `agent`) to anyone who may call the API. It never shows a folder on the machine.

## Routine reports

`routines/` holds one folder per routine, `<name>-<first 8 of its id>`, with the report files the routine saved. Nothing in it is ever deleted automatically: a person removes old reports. They are part of a backup. See [routines](/next/conventions/routines/index.html#reports).

## Logs

The `logs/` folder of the data home holds the agent's log files, one per area. They are not part of a backup. See [logs](/next/conventions/logs/index.html).

## `bxAgents data`

```bash
bxAgents data [--json]
```

Prints the data home and where it came from, the size of the database and each folder, and the volumes with their modes.

## Backups

```bash
bxAgents backup [--to=FILE]
bxAgents restore FILE [--home=DIR] [--force]
```

`backup` writes one zip with the chat database, `files/`, `skills/` and `routines/`, plus a small `backup.json`. Without `--to` it goes in the home's `backups/` folder as `backup-<date>-<time>.zip`. The database is copied whole with SQLite's own `VACUUM INTO`, so it is safe to run while a server is using it. Volumes are not included: they are your folders.

`restore` puts a backup back. What was there is kept beside it as `chat.db.before-restore`, `files.before-restore` and `skills.before-restore` for one restore; the next restore replaces them. It stops when a server or chat looks to have the database open (SQLite leaves a `-wal` file while one does), unless you pass `--force`. `--home` restores into another data home. A zip with an entry that is not part of a backup, or that tries to leave the home, is refused before anything is changed.

title: deploy/
body: deploy/ Each deploy/*.bx / .json entry describes one deployment target attempt - a place to ship a built/packaged project to: // deploy/production.bx class { function configure() { return { target : "digitalocean", appName : "my-agent", region : "nyc", registry : { type : "ghcr", repository : "myorg/my-agent" }, httpPort : 8080, instanceSize : "apps-s-1vcpu-1gb", envs : [ { key : "OPENAI_API_KEY", scope : "RUN_TIME", type : "SECRET" } ] }; } } Run it with: bxAgents deploy --name=production deploy/ is deliberately not validated on every build - deployment config never affects the generated ColdBox app or its manifest, so checking it on every build would be pure overhead for projects that never deploy. It's only discovered and validated when deploy actually runs. The simplest case needs no deploy/ folder at all: bxAgents deploy --destination=/path/to/somewhere is shorthand for the local target. Every other target needs more configuration than a couple of flags can reasonably carry, so it requires a named deploy/* entry ( --name=<entry> ). Targets Every target implements the same IDeploymentTarget interface ( struct function deploy( config, context ) ) - the target field picks which one runs. local Copy the newest .bxa to a destination directory. No deploy/ folder needed. ssh Ship over scp , optionally restart the remote service over ssh . docker Build an image from .build and push it to a registry. digitalocean Push-and-minimal-provision against the DigitalOcean App Platform API. ftp / sftp Ship the newest .bxa to a remote directory over plain FTP or SFTP. local Copies the newest packaged .bxa (by file modification time, never a lexical filename sort - v9.0.0 would otherwise sort after v10.0.0 ) to a destination directory. { target: "local", destination: "/path/to/somewhere" } Requires a prior bxAgents package . ssh Ships the newest .bxa to a bare server over scp , then optionally runs a remote restart command over ssh . { target : "ssh", host : "example.com", username : "deploy", remotePath : "/srv/apps/my-agent", identityFile : "/home/me/.ssh/id_rsa", // optional restartCommand : "systemctl restart my-agent" // optional } Requires a prior bxAgents package . Shells out to the real scp / ssh binaries - they must be installed and on PATH . docker Builds a Docker image from .build (the app, its libraries, the web root and the runtime home) and pushes it to a container registry, shelling out to the real docker CLI. { target : "docker", registry : { type : "ghcr", repository : "myorg/my-agent" }, // type: "dockerhub" | "ghcr" | "docr" tag : "1.0.0" // optional, defaults to "latest" } Requires a prior bxAgents build (not package - it builds straight from .build ). The built-in Dockerfile template is based on the real, published ortussolutions/boxlang:miniserver image - override it entirely by adding your own deploy/Dockerfile , or point at a different one via dockerfile: "/absolute/path" . It is: FROM ortussolutions/boxlang:miniserver ENV APP_DIR=/srv/bxapp ENV BOXLANG_HOME=/srv/bxapp/runtime COPY . /srv/bxapp RUN sed -i 's/"host": *"[^"]*"/"host": "0.0.0.0"/' /srv/bxapp/miniserver.json EXPOSE 8080 Why `/srv/bxapp` and not `/app` The image's entrypoint does cd $APP_DIR and starts the miniserver there, where it reads miniserver.json (web root public , engine config runtime/boxlang.json , home runtime ); runtime/ is the BoxLang home so that only the bundled bx-agents module (internal alias bxagents ) loads. A .dockerignore written into .build keeps the manifest, the work folders and what a running server wrote into runtime/ out of the image. Do not install the app under a folder named /app : the runtime config maps /app to the ColdBox app folder, so BoxLang takes the absolute path /app/app/config/bxai-settings.json for a path under that mapping, looks at /app/app/app/config/... and the first request fails with "Failed to load application descriptor". This recipe was built and run: /__bxagents/health , /chat/ and its assets answer 200, and /config/... , /project/Agent.yml , /app/config/bxai-settings.json and /runtime/boxlang.json answer 404. Not verified: an actual model call from inside the container. docker login only runs when both DOCKER_USERNAME and DOCKER_PASSWORD are set in the environment - a registry an already-authenticated local Docker daemon can reach needs neither. digitalocean Deploys to a DigitalOcean App Platform app - "push and minimal provision": builds/pushes the image exactly like docker (reuses the same registry config shape), then either redeploys an existing app or creates one from scratch if it doesn't exist yet. { target : "digitalocean", appName : "my-agent", region : "nyc", // optional, defaults to "nyc" registry : { type : "docr", repository : "myorg/my-agent" }, // "namespace/repo" form httpPort : 8080, // optional, defaults to 8080 instanceSize : "apps-s-1vcpu-1gb", // optional, defaults to "apps-s-1vcpu-1gb" instanceCount : 1, // optional, defaults to 1 tag : "1.0.0", // optional, image tag, defaults to "latest" envs : [ { key : "OPENAI_API_KEY", scope : "RUN_TIME", type : "SECRET" } ] // optional } registry.repository must be in namespace/repo form (e.g. myorg/my-agent ) - the DigitalOcean App Spec's image block needs the namespace and repository as separate fields. Requires a prior bxAgents build . An existing app is found by name ( GET /v2/apps , filtered client-side on spec.name ) rather than remembering a local app-ID file, so this works identically from any machine or CI runner with no local state to go stale. ftp / sftp Ships the newest .bxa to a remote directory over plain FTP or SFTP, via the real bx:ftp component - bundled with BxAgents as a nested module. remotePath is a remote directory - the uploaded file keeps its own name, the same convention ssh 's scp target uses. // deploy/ftp-production.bx { target : "ftp", host : "ftp.example.com", username : "deploy", passwordEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_FTP_PASSWORD", remotePath : "/uploads/my-agent", port : 21, // optional, defaults to 21 passive : true, // optional, defaults to true timeout : 30, // optional, seconds, defaults to 30 proxyServer : "proxy.company.com:8080" // optional } // deploy/sftp-production.bx { target : "sftp", host : "sftp.example.com", username : "deploy", key : "/home/me/.ssh/id_rsa", // passwordEnvVar OR key required passphraseEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_SFTP_KEY_PASSPHRASE", // optional, only if the key itself is passphrase-protected fingerprint : "SHA256:...", // optional host key verification remotePath : "/uploads/my-agent", port : 22, // optional, defaults to 22 timeout : 30 // optional, seconds, defaults to 30 } Requires a prior bxAgents package . ftp requires a passwordEnvVar ; sftp accepts either a passwordEnvVar or a key (SSH private key file path). passwordEnvVar / passphraseEnvVar name environment variables holding the real secret - never the secret value itself - resolved live at deploy time. The variable they name must sit in the BXAGENTS_ namespace ( ^BXAGENTS_[A-Z0-9_]+$ ); anything else is rejected with a BxAgents.InvalidDeployConfig error. That keeps a deploy entry - which is plain data, and easy to wave through in review - from naming an unrelated secret already in the environment (say a provider API key) and having it sent to whatever host the same entry points at. key stays a plain path, since it's already not secret material itself. Every bx:ftp action throws on failure (connection refused, auth rejected, a negative server reply) rather than returning a soft failure - this target catches that and re-throws it as a clear BxAgents.DeployFailed , always closing the connection afterward even on error. Secrets stay external No target ever reads a secret (API token, SSH key, registry password) from deploy/* config - every credential is resolved from an environment variable at deploy time, matching this project's existing rule that provider API keys are never embedded in a build or package (see Deployment & Secrets ): Target Env var(s) ssh none required - identityFile is a path to a key file you manage yourself docker DOCKER_USERNAME , DOCKER_PASSWORD (both optional - only used if set) digitalocean DOCKER_USERNAME / DOCKER_PASSWORD (for the image push) + DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN (required) ftp / sftp whichever BXAGENTS_ -prefixed env var(s) passwordEnvVar / passphraseEnvVar name - the entry itself only ever holds the env var's NAME, never its value ( key is a path, same as ssh 's identityFile ) Validation target must be one of local , ssh , docker , digitalocean , ftp , sftp . Entry names must be unique across deploy/*.bx and deploy/*.json . Each target's required fields (above) are checked when deploy runs - local needs destination , ssh / ftp / sftp need host / username / remotePath (the same field name across all three), docker / digitalocean need registry.repository , digitalocean also needs appName , ftp also needs passwordEnvVar , sftp also needs passwordEnvVar or key .

ftp / sftp Ship the newest `.bxa` to a remote directory over plain FTP or SFTP.](#ftp--sftp)
### `local` Copies the newest packaged `.bxa` (by file modification time, never a lexical filename sort - `v9.0.0` would otherwise sort after `v10.0.0`) to a destination directory. ```javascript { target: "local", destination: "/path/to/somewhere" } ``` Requires a prior `bxAgents package`. ### `ssh` Ships the newest `.bxa` to a bare server over `scp`, then optionally runs a remote restart command over `ssh`. ```javascript { target : "ssh", host : "example.com", username : "deploy", remotePath : "/srv/apps/my-agent", identityFile : "/home/me/.ssh/id_rsa", // optional restartCommand : "systemctl restart my-agent" // optional } ``` Requires a prior `bxAgents package`. Shells out to the real `scp`/`ssh` binaries - they must be installed and on `PATH`. ### `docker` Builds a Docker image from `.build` (the app, its libraries, the web root and the runtime home) and pushes it to a container registry, shelling out to the real `docker` CLI. ```javascript { target : "docker", registry : { type : "ghcr", repository : "myorg/my-agent" }, // type: "dockerhub" | "ghcr" | "docr" tag : "1.0.0" // optional, defaults to "latest" } ``` Requires a prior `bxAgents build` (not `package` - it builds straight from `.build`). The built-in Dockerfile template is based on the real, published [`ortussolutions/boxlang:miniserver`](https://boxlang.ortusbooks.com/getting-started/running-boxlang/docker) image - override it entirely by adding your own `deploy/Dockerfile`, or point at a different one via `dockerfile: "/absolute/path"`. It is: ```dockerfile FROM ortussolutions/boxlang:miniserver ENV APP_DIR=/srv/bxapp ENV BOXLANG_HOME=/srv/bxapp/runtime COPY . /srv/bxapp RUN sed -i 's/"host": *"[^"]*"/"host": "0.0.0.0"/' /srv/bxapp/miniserver.json EXPOSE 8080 ``` > **Why \`/srv/bxapp\` and not \`/app\`** > > The image's entrypoint does `cd $APP_DIR` and starts the miniserver there, where it reads `miniserver.json` (web root `public`, engine config `runtime/boxlang.json`, home `runtime`); `runtime/` is the BoxLang home so that only the bundled `bx-agents` module (internal alias `bxagents`) loads. A `.dockerignore` written into `.build` keeps the manifest, the work folders and what a running server wrote into `runtime/` out of the image. **Do not install the app under a folder named `/app`:** the runtime config maps `/app` to the ColdBox app folder, so BoxLang takes the absolute path `/app/app/config/bxai-settings.json` for a path under that mapping, looks at `/app/app/app/config/...` and the first request fails with "Failed to load application descriptor". This recipe was built and run: `/__bxagents/health`, `/chat/` and its assets answer 200, and `/config/...`, `/project/Agent.yml`, `/app/config/bxai-settings.json` and `/runtime/boxlang.json` answer 404. Not verified: an actual model call from inside the container. `docker login` only runs when both `DOCKER_USERNAME` and `DOCKER_PASSWORD` are set in the environment - a registry an already-authenticated local Docker daemon can reach needs neither. ### `digitalocean` Deploys to a [DigitalOcean App Platform](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform) app - "push and minimal provision": builds/pushes the image exactly like `docker` (reuses the same `registry` config shape), then either redeploys an existing app or creates one from scratch if it doesn't exist yet. ```javascript { target : "digitalocean", appName : "my-agent", region : "nyc", // optional, defaults to "nyc" registry : { type : "docr", repository : "myorg/my-agent" }, // "namespace/repo" form httpPort : 8080, // optional, defaults to 8080 instanceSize : "apps-s-1vcpu-1gb", // optional, defaults to "apps-s-1vcpu-1gb" instanceCount : 1, // optional, defaults to 1 tag : "1.0.0", // optional, image tag, defaults to "latest" envs : [ { key : "OPENAI_API_KEY", scope : "RUN_TIME", type : "SECRET" } ] // optional } ``` `registry.repository` must be in `namespace/repo` form (e.g. `myorg/my-agent`) - the DigitalOcean App Spec's `image` block needs the namespace and repository as separate fields. Requires a prior `bxAgents build`. An existing app is found by name (`GET /v2/apps`, filtered client-side on `spec.name`) rather than remembering a local app-ID file, so this works identically from any machine or CI runner with no local state to go stale. ### `ftp` / `sftp` Ships the newest `.bxa` to a remote directory over plain FTP or SFTP, via the real [`bx:ftp`](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-ftp) component - bundled with BxAgents as a nested module. `remotePath` is a remote **directory** - the uploaded file keeps its own name, the same convention `ssh`'s `scp` target uses. ```javascript // deploy/ftp-production.bx { target : "ftp", host : "ftp.example.com", username : "deploy", passwordEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_FTP_PASSWORD", remotePath : "/uploads/my-agent", port : 21, // optional, defaults to 21 passive : true, // optional, defaults to true timeout : 30, // optional, seconds, defaults to 30 proxyServer : "proxy.company.com:8080" // optional } ``` ```javascript // deploy/sftp-production.bx { target : "sftp", host : "sftp.example.com", username : "deploy", key : "/home/me/.ssh/id_rsa", // passwordEnvVar OR key required passphraseEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_SFTP_KEY_PASSPHRASE", // optional, only if the key itself is passphrase-protected fingerprint : "SHA256:...", // optional host key verification remotePath : "/uploads/my-agent", port : 22, // optional, defaults to 22 timeout : 30 // optional, seconds, defaults to 30 } ``` Requires a prior `bxAgents package`. `ftp` requires a `passwordEnvVar`; `sftp` accepts either a `passwordEnvVar` or a `key` (SSH private key file path). `passwordEnvVar`/`passphraseEnvVar` name environment variables holding the real secret - **never the secret value itself** - resolved live at deploy time. The variable they name must sit in the `BXAGENTS_` namespace (`^BXAGENTS_[A-Z0-9_]+$`); anything else is rejected with a `BxAgents.InvalidDeployConfig` error. That keeps a deploy entry - which is plain data, and easy to wave through in review - from naming an unrelated secret already in the environment (say a provider API key) and having it sent to whatever host the same entry points at. `key` stays a plain path, since it's already not secret material itself. Every `bx:ftp` action throws on failure (connection refused, auth rejected, a negative server reply) rather than returning a soft failure - this target catches that and re-throws it as a clear `BxAgents.DeployFailed`, always closing the connection afterward even on error. ## Secrets stay external No target ever reads a secret (API token, SSH key, registry password) from `deploy/*` config - every credential is resolved from an environment variable at deploy time, matching this project's existing rule that provider API keys are never embedded in a build or package (see [Deployment \& Secrets](/next/deployment-and-secrets/index.html)): | Target | Env var(s) | |----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `ssh` | none required - `identityFile` is a path to a key file you manage yourself | | `docker` | `DOCKER_USERNAME`, `DOCKER_PASSWORD` (both optional - only used if set) | | `digitalocean` | `DOCKER_USERNAME`/`DOCKER_PASSWORD` (for the image push) + `DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN` (required) | | `ftp` / `sftp` | whichever `BXAGENTS_`-prefixed env var(s) `passwordEnvVar`/`passphraseEnvVar` name - the entry itself only ever holds the env var's NAME, never its value (`key` is a path, same as `ssh`'s `identityFile`) | ## Validation * `target` must be one of `local`, `ssh`, `docker`, `digitalocean`, `ftp`, `sftp`. * Entry names must be unique across `deploy/*.bx` and `deploy/*.json`. * Each target's required fields (above) are checked when `deploy` runs - `local` needs `destination`, `ssh`/`ftp`/`sftp` need `host`/`username`/`remotePath` (the same field name across all three), `docker`/`digitalocean` need `registry.repository`, `digitalocean` also needs `appName`, `ftp` also needs `passwordEnvVar`, `sftp` also needs `passwordEnvVar` or `key`.

body:
Deployment & Secrets Secrets never enter the artifact - they are supplied to the process , at the far right of this chain: flowchart LR P["your project"] -->|"bxAgents build"| B[".build/
app/ public/ lib/ runtime/"] B -->|"bxAgents package"| A["dist/name-version.bxa
+ .sha256 + redacted manifest.json"] A -->|"bxAgents deploy"| T["a target:
local / ssh / ftp / sftp
docker / digitalocean"] T --> RUN["boxlang-miniserver runs in the unzipped folder"] ENV["environment variables
OPENAI_API_KEY, CLAUDE_API_KEY,
every *EnvVar a gateway names"] -->|"read at RUNTIME by bx-ai"| RUN style A fill:#eaf6ec,stroke:#155724 style ENV fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#856404 Nothing on the left of ENV ever holds a secret value: .env /dotfiles are excluded from the zip unconditionally, and the manifest is redacted on top of never carrying one. Packaging bxAgents package zips the built app into a portable .bxa artifact. What is zipped is the packaging set of the ColdBox BoxLang template : app/ , lib/ , public/ , runtime/ (without its logs, class cache and the other files a running server creates in its home), boxlang_modules/ and miniserver.json , all from .build/ (see what is in .build ). manifest.json and the build's work folders are not part of it. bxAgents package --version=1.0.0 produces, in dist/ : {agentName}-{version}.bxa - the zipped app {agentName}-{version}.bxa.sha256 - its checksum manifest.json - a redacted copy of the build manifest (see below) Packaging twice in a row over the same build produces byte-identical zip bytes (deterministic entry order/timestamps) - useful for verifying a CI-built artifact matches a locally-built one. The .bxa is relocatable : it carries every file the agent reads at runtime (including each agent node's own instructions.md , copied into agent/ at build time), and the generated agent/GeneratedAgentFactory.bx resolves those paths relative to its own location on disk rather than the absolute paths of the machine that built it. So a .bxa built on CI runs unchanged when unzipped anywhere else - which also means a .bxaignore broad enough to match *.md will strip the agent's own instructions out of the artifact. package requires a prior build (it reads .build/manifest.json ) and refuses to run - producing no .bxa - if manifestVersion is unset or malformed. Excluding files: .bxaignore An optional .bxaignore at the project root, one glob pattern per line ( # -prefixed lines are comments), excludes matching paths from the packaged .bxa . Patterns are matched against paths inside .build (so app/skills/old/ , not skills/old/ , which is where they were matched before the app and the web root were split): a pattern with no / matches at any depth, one with a / is anchored at the root of .build , a trailing / names a folder and everything under it, and * also crosses / . # .bxaignore *.log scratch/ This is on top of a hard-coded, always-on exclusion of .env / .env.* /dotfiles at the packaging layer - even if .bxaignore doesn't mention them, and even if they somehow ended up inside .build , they never make it into the zip. Secret redaction Secrets are never written into manifest.json in the first place - the manifest's agent block only ever contains safe, structural fields ( name , description , model , environment ). As defense-in-depth, package additionally walks the manifest recursively and replaces any struct key that looks like a secret with [REDACTED] : (apikey | api_key | token | secret | password)$ (case-insensitive, any prefix) This guards against a future field - or a caller passing a richer struct into package some other way - accidentally leaking a value, even though today's manifest never puts one there to begin with. Where real secrets live BxAgents never resolves, stores, or embeds provider API keys, tokens, or passwords anywhere in a build or package. That's entirely bx-ai's job, at runtime : it reads them from the process environment following its own _API_KEY -style convention (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY , CLAUDE_API_KEY ). Set them however you normally manage secrets for a deployed process - an OS environment variable or your platform's secret manager. For local development, BoxLang and boxlang-miniserver both load a .env from the project root themselves, so bxAgents new 's .env is the easy place for them; BxAgents never reads, copies or embeds it, and it is never committed (the scaffolded .gitignore covers it) or packaged. A deployed .bxa has no .env , so give that process real environment variables. export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... bxAgents serve Variables BxAgents reads itself None of these holds a provider secret. BXAGENTS_TOKEN is the one credential, and it is only ever read from the environment of the machine you type on. Variable Used by Effect BX_AGENTS_ENV build The active environment when --environment is not given (default development ). See Environments . BXAGENTS_DB the app, chat , token , notes , sessions , stats The chat database file. serve sets it to the chat.db of the data home ( ~/.bxagents//chat.db by default). Without it, the app asks the data home for the file, so a deployed app keeps it in its own data home too; database.path is only the fallback for an agent with no name. See the SQLite store . BXAGENTS_TOKEN chat --connect The token to send, instead of --token . BXAGENTS_USER_CONFIG build , the app at start, chat , extensions Another file in place of ~/.bxagents/Agent.yml , the person's file for every agent. BXAGENTS_SKILLS_URL skills Another skills registry, instead of --registry . BXAGENTS_BANNER , BXAGENTS_BANNER_THEME --help , new off hides the banner; a theme name pins its colors. BXAGENTS_ plus a name deploy The only prefix a deploy/ entry may name for a password or passphrase ( passwordEnvVar , passphraseEnvVar ). Secrets people hand to a running agent Environment variables are for what you deploy with. For a key or login that a person hands to a running agent (an API key for Gmail, a ticket system, a customer's own token), use the vault : values are sealed in the chat database, added from the terminal chat, the web page or bxAgents vault , and read by the runtime at the moment a tool or MCP server needs one. They are never part of a build, a package or the manifest. Set BXAGENTS_VAULT_KEY in the environment of the deployed process so the key does not sit beside the database. A service that asks each person to sign in ( connect ) seals the tokens it is given with the same key. Set BXAGENTS_PUBLIC_URL to the address people reach the server at ( https://agent.example.com ), and register /__bxagents/connect/callback with the provider: that is where the browser comes back after a sign in. Deploying bxAgents deploy --destination=/path/to/somewhere # local, flag-only shorthand bxAgents deploy --name=production # any target, via deploy/production.bx Six pluggable targets ship out of the box - local (copy the newest .bxa somewhere), ssh (ship it to a bare server), ftp / sftp (ship it via the real bx-ftp module, bundled with BxAgents), docker (build/push a container image), and digitalocean (deploy to a DigitalOcean App Platform app) - see deploy/ for the full config shape of each and CLI Reference for the CLI flags. No target ever reads a secret from deploy/* config - credentials (registry passwords, SSH keys, the DigitalOcean API token) are always resolved from environment variables at deploy time, the same "secrets stay external" rule as everywhere else in this doc. See deploy/ for the exact env var each target expects. To run a packaged .bxa somewhere else manually: unzip it into a folder (its path must not hold a space: the boxlang-miniserver launcher script does not quote it), go into that folder, and start the server there with the runtime as its home, setting whatever secret environment variables that deployment needs: cd /srv/my-agent BOXLANG_HOME="$PWD/runtime" boxlang-miniserver miniserver.json miniserver.json names everything by paths relative to the folder it is in ( webRoot: public , configPath: runtime/boxlang.json , serverHome: runtime ), so the same file serves the app wherever it is unzipped, and only public/ is reachable from outside. It binds 127.0.0.1:8080 as packaged: edit host (and port ) for the machine it runs on, or put a reverse proxy in front.

See [Environments](/next/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#environments). | | `BXAGENTS_DB` | the app, `chat`, `token`, `notes`, `sessions`, `stats` | The chat database file. `serve` sets it to the `chat.db` of the [data home](/next/conventions/data/index.html) (`~/.bxagents//chat.db` by default). Without it, the app asks the data home for the file, so a deployed app keeps it in its own data home too; `database.path` is only the fallback for an agent with no name. See [the SQLite store](/next/conventions/web-ui/index.html#the-sqlite-store). | | `BXAGENTS_TOKEN` | `chat --connect` | The token to send, instead of `--token`. | | `BXAGENTS_USER_CONFIG` | `build`, the app at start, `chat`, `extensions` | Another file in place of `~/.bxagents/Agent.yml`, the person's file for every agent. | | `BXAGENTS_SKILLS_URL` | `skills` | Another skills registry, instead of `--registry`. | | `BXAGENTS_BANNER`, `BXAGENTS_BANNER_THEME` | `--help`, `new` | `off` hides the banner; a theme name pins its colors. | | `BXAGENTS_` plus a name | `deploy` | The only prefix a `deploy/` entry may name for a password or passphrase (`passwordEnvVar`, `passphraseEnvVar`). | ## Secrets people hand to a running agent Environment variables are for what you deploy with.
