# Routines and Reports

A **routine** is a prompt the agent runs on a schedule, as the person who made it. "Every weekday at 9, check the
build and tell me what broke" is a routine. Nobody writes a file: a person asks the agent, approves the tool
call, and the agent keeps the routine in the chat database. A run can save what it found as a **report**, a file you
read later.
> **What you will build**
>
> A routine that runs while the app is served, a report it saves, and the ways to read both. About 25 minutes.
> It continues from [The Agent Asks First](/next/course/approvals/index.html), where you made the routine `weekly-report`.

## Routines are not schedulers

BoxLang has its own scheduler, and BxAgents lets a developer use it from `schedules/*.bx` (the next lesson). A routine
is for the people who use the agent:

|              |            `schedules/*.bx`            |                        Routine                         |
|--------------|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| Who makes it | The developer, in a file               | Anyone, by asking the agent                            |
| Lives        | In the project, shipped with the agent | In the chat database, per person                       |
| Runs as      | The app                                | The person who made it, with their notes and approvals |
| Changed by   | Editing the file and rebuilding        | Asking the agent, while the app runs                   |

## 1. The routine from the last lesson

```bash
cd ~/bxagents-course/acme-support
bxAgents routines list
```

```text
weekly-report         every 5 minutes           not run yet           next <anything>
```

A schedule is stored as a 5-field cron expression (`0 9 * * 1-5`) or an interval (`every 30m`, `every 2h`), and
every answer reads it back in words, so a mistake is seen straight away. The prompt it will run is `report`; the
scripted model answers a routine run by saving a report (its rule listens for the sentence every run starts with,
"This is a scheduled routine").

## 2. Run it

Routines are started by a **heartbeat**: a scheduler BxAgents adds to the app that wakes every minute, looks for
routines that are due, and starts them. That heartbeat only exists in a served app. Serve it (Terminal 3):

```bash
cd ~/bxagents-course/acme-support
bxAgents serve --port=8791
```

Instead of waiting five minutes, mark the routine due. `run` does not run anything itself; it makes the routine due
at the next heartbeat:

```bash
bxAgents routines run weekly-report
```

```text
...
Marked due routine weekly-report. Next run <anything>
It starts at the next minute of a served app, not from this command.
```

Wait up to a minute. The server's output (Terminal 3) shows the routine start, save a report and finish, and the
run is a normal turn of the agent as you, in a conversation of its own:

```bash
bxAgents routines list
```

```text
weekly-report<anything>every 5 minutes<anything>ok<anything>
```

> **Not served, not run**
>
> From a terminal that is not serving the app, `routines run` marks the routine and nothing starts it. If a
> routine never runs, check that the app is running (and `bxAgents logs heartbeat`).

## 3. Read the report

A routine saves what it found with the `report_save` tool. Reports go in the data home under
`routines/<name>-<id>/`, are never overwritten (a name already used becomes `report-2.md`) and are never deleted
by the agent, only by a person:

```bash
bxAgents routines reports weekly-report
bxAgents routines report weekly-report weekly.md
```

```text
weekly.md<anything>62 bytes<anything>
# Weekly report

No open orders. Returns are free for 30 days.
```

The run's conversation is in the list too, named `routine-weekly-report-<id>`, and reads like any other. Open the
web app's **Routines** page for the same things with buttons: each row shows the status in words, the schedule in
words, the next and last run, and **Run now** , **Pause** , **Edit** , **Reports** and **Delete**.

![The Routines page: three routines, one paused, with the schedule in words and the next run](/next/assets/webui/webui-routines.png)

![The reports of one routine, with a report open](/next/assets/webui/webui-routine-reports.png)

## 4. Make, pause and delete one from a script

Asking the agent is the usual way, and it needs your approval. A program, and the web page's **New routine** , can
make one directly through the API, as the same person. (The CLI's `routines add --schedule="every 1h"` does not work on
the BoxLang 1.19.0 launcher yet, because the schedule has a space; see
[Quoting flag values](/next/cli-reference/index.html#quoting-flag-values).)

```bash
curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"daily-check","schedule":"every 1h","prompt":"report"}' http://127.0.0.1:8791/__bxagents/routines > /dev/null
bxAgents routines pause daily-check
bxAgents routines list
```

```text
...
Paused routine daily-check. Next run <anything>
daily-check<anything>every hour<anything>paused<anything>
weekly-report<anything>every 5 minutes<anything>ok<anything>
```

```bash
bxAgents routines delete daily-check --yes
bxAgents routines list
```

```text
...
Deleted routine.
weekly-report<anything>every 5 minutes<anything>ok<anything>
```

Deleting a routine keeps its conversation and its reports.

## What the heartbeat guarantees

* **Runs as the person.** The run uses their notes and their approvals. A routine cannot make or change routines (a run is refused the `routine_*` tools).
* **No overlap.** A routine still running is skipped, and the skip is logged.
* **Three failures in a row pause it.** `routines resume <name>` (or the Resume button) starts it again and clears the failures. A run that stops for an approval shows as *waiting for approval* ; after `approvalTimeout` it is cancelled and counts as a failure.
* **Catch-up is once.** If the server was down when a routine was due, it runs once on start, never once per missed time.
* **Where the answer goes.** By default into the routine's own conversation. A routine made from a chat platform can send a summary back to that chat, and a person can name a gateway (`gateway:telegram`).

The settings (`maxPerUser`, `minInterval`, `timezone`, `maxReportSize` and the rest) are in the
[routines reference](/next/conventions/routines/index.html#turn-it-on). `routines.log` and `heartbeat.log` record each
routine made, changed, run, skipped and failed, never the prompt or the text of a report; the
[operating lesson](/next/course/operating-it/index.html) reads them.

## Checkpoint

Nothing in the project changed in this lesson. In the data home there is one routine, `weekly-report`, and one report.

Full reference: [routines](/next/conventions/routines/index.html) and [the CLI reference](/next/cli-reference/index.html#routines).

Next: [Scheduling Background Work](/next/course/16-scheduling-background-work/index.html)

body: Scaffolding Your First Agent In A Model That Needs No Key you ran one command and got a project: bxAgents new acme-support --model=openai-compatible/fast-model --skipInstall --no-banner This lesson is the tour of what that command made. --model is a provider/model slug (you'll see exactly how this gets parsed in The Agent Definition - Agent.yml ). Pass it for a script-friendly run: without --model , at a terminal, new asks you questions instead (see new wizard ). --name and --description are optional; --name defaults to the target directory's own name. new refuses to run if the target already contains an Agent.yml or Agent.bx . The wizard At a terminal, bxAgents new my-agent (no --model ) opens a full-screen wizard. It asks what the agent should do: its model, tools, memory, MCP servers, channels (web chat, Slack, Telegram and so on), how people sign in, and where it deploys. Esc goes back one question and Ctrl+C creates nothing. One question picks a template, the shape the project starts from, and your other answers are added on top of it: a template is a preset, not a limit. The last screen prints the one-line command that builds the same project without questions, so a script can repeat it. Pass --model (or --no-wizard ) to skip the questions. See the new wizard for every question and flag. What gets created acme-support/ ├── Agent.yml ├── box.json ├── instructions.md ├── tools/ ├── skills/ ├── subagents/ ├── gateways/ ├── schedules/ ├── mcp/ ├── interceptors/ ├── modules/ └── tests/ └── specs/ └── AgentSpec.bx Plus a .env (commented API key stubs only; it deliberately does not set BOXLANG_HOME ), a .gitignore (it ignores .build/ , dist/ , .env , lib/ and data/chat.db* , among others; the chat database now lives in the agent's data home, ~/.bxagents/<agent name>/ , outside the project, so that last line only matters for a project that already keeps one in data/ ) and a few dotfiles ( .boxlang.json , .editorconfig , .bxlint.json , .gitattributes , .markdownlint.json ) - new never overwrites them if they already exist. BoxLang loads the .env from the project root itself, so this is where secrets live: the wizard and add write an empty line for each key your choices need (a provider key, a bot token), and the files that use it hold only the variable's name. Every convention folder is created empty . You add files to the ones your agent actually needs and leave the rest alone - an empty tools/ folder has zero effect on the generated app. Agent.yml looks like this (Pass --description and new adds a description: line.) # Your agent. Most agents need nothing more than this file and instructions.md. # For code in the definition (hooks, dynamic instructions), scaffold with --class. name: acme-support provider: openai-compatible model: fast-model environments: # `bxAgents test` builds against this override by default (see # BaseAgentSpec.bx) so a fresh project's tests need no API key or # network access - swap the model to test against a real provider. test: model: mock/mock-model That is the whole agent definition - more on each key in The Agent Definition - Agent.yml . If you need code in the definition, pass --class and new scaffolds a class-based Agent.bx instead (also covered at the end of The Agent Definition ). The test suite new can also run box install in the project root (its box.json lists TestBox, installed into lib/testbox ), so bxAgents test ( Testing Your Agent ) works immediately. This is best-effort: if box isn't on PATH or the install fails, new still succeeds and tells you to run it yourself. You passed --skipInstall , so nothing was installed yet, and nothing in the next lessons needs it. Try it Look at what is there, then ask for a tool without writing it. add shows what it would write when you pass --dry-run , and writes nothing: cd ~/bxagents-course/acme-support ls bxAgents add tool Orders --function=orderStatus --dry-run Would create tools/Orders.bx ... Later you can add to a project without editing files by hand: bxAgents add tool , add skill , add subagent , add gateway , add schedule and the other add kinds ask a few questions and write the files for you. The next lessons walk through what is actually required to run it. Checkpoint Nothing changed in acme-support/ in this lesson: it is the project from the last one. Next: The Agent Definition - Agent.yml

# Scaffolding Your First Agent

In [A Model That Needs No Key](/next/course/practice-model/index.html) you ran one command and got a project:

```bash
bxAgents new acme-support --model=openai-compatible/fast-model --skipInstall --no-banner
```

This lesson is the tour of what that command made. `--model` is a `provider/model` slug (you'll see exactly how
this gets parsed in [The Agent Definition - Agent.yml](/next/course/05-agent-bx/index.html)). Pass it for a script-friendly run: without
`--model`, at a terminal, `new` asks you questions instead (see [`new` wizard](/next/guides/new-wizard/index.html)).
`--name` and `--description` are optional;
`--name` defaults to the target directory's own name. `new` refuses to run if the
target already contains an `Agent.yml` or `Agent.bx`.

## The wizard

At a terminal, `bxAgents new my-agent` (no `--model`) opens a full-screen wizard. It asks what
the agent should do: its model, tools, memory, MCP servers, channels (web chat, Slack, Telegram
and so on), how people sign in, and where it deploys. Esc goes back one question and Ctrl+C
creates nothing. One question picks a template, the shape the project starts from, and
your other answers are added on top of it: a template is a preset, not a limit. The last screen
prints the one-line command that builds the same project without questions, so a script can
repeat it. Pass `--model` (or `--no-wizard`) to skip the questions. See the
[`new` wizard](/next/guides/new-wizard/index.html) for every question and flag.

## What gets created

```text
acme-support/
├── Agent.yml
├── box.json
├── instructions.md
├── tools/
├── skills/
├── subagents/
├── gateways/
├── schedules/
├── mcp/
├── interceptors/
├── modules/
└── tests/
    └── specs/
        └── AgentSpec.bx
```

Plus a `.env` (commented API key stubs only; it deliberately does not set `BOXLANG_HOME`), a `.gitignore` (it ignores `.build/`, `dist/`, `.env`, `lib/` and `data/chat.db*`, among others; the chat database now lives in the agent's data home, `~/.bxagents/<agent name>/`, outside the project, so that last line only matters for a project that already keeps one in `data/`)
and a few dotfiles (`.boxlang.json`, `.editorconfig`, `.bxlint.json`, `.gitattributes`,
`.markdownlint.json`) - `new` never overwrites them if they already exist. BoxLang loads the `.env` from the project root itself, so
this is where secrets live: the wizard and `add` write an empty line for each key your choices
need (a provider key, a bot token), and the files that use it hold only the variable's name.

Every convention folder is created **empty** . You add files to the ones your agent
actually needs and leave the rest alone - an empty `tools/` folder has zero effect on
the generated app.

## `Agent.yml` looks like this

(Pass `--description` and `new` adds a `description:` line.)

```yaml
# Your agent. Most agents need nothing more than this file and instructions.md.
# For code in the definition (hooks, dynamic instructions), scaffold with --class.
name: acme-support
provider: openai-compatible
model: fast-model

environments:
  # `bxAgents test` builds against this override by default (see
  # BaseAgentSpec.bx) so a fresh project's tests need no API key or
  # network access - swap the model to test against a real provider.
  test:
    model: mock/mock-model
```

That is the whole agent definition - more on each key in [The Agent Definition - Agent.yml](/next/course/05-agent-bx/index.html).
If you need code in the definition, pass `--class` and `new` scaffolds a class-based
`Agent.bx` instead (also covered at the end of [The Agent Definition](/next/course/05-agent-bx/index.html)).

## The test suite

`new` can also run `box install` in the project root (its `box.json` lists TestBox, installed into `lib/testbox`),
so `bxAgents test` ([Testing Your Agent](/next/course/19-testing-your-agent/index.html)) works immediately. This is best-effort: if
`box` isn't on `PATH` or the install fails, `new` still succeeds and tells you to run it yourself. You passed
`--skipInstall`, so nothing was installed yet, and nothing in the next lessons needs it.

## Try it

Look at what is there, then ask for a tool without writing it. `add` shows what it would write when you pass
`--dry-run`, and writes nothing:

```bash
cd ~/bxagents-course/acme-support
ls
```

```bash
bxAgents add tool Orders --function=orderStatus --dry-run
```

```text
Would create tools/Orders.bx
...
```

Later you can add to a project without editing files by hand: `bxAgents add tool`, `add skill`, `add subagent`,
`add gateway`, `add schedule` and the other `add` kinds ask a few questions and write the files for you. The
next lessons walk through what is actually required to run it.

## Checkpoint

Nothing changed in `acme-support/` in this lesson: it is the project from the last one.

Next: [The Agent Definition - Agent.yml](/next/course/05-agent-bx/index.html)

# schedules/

Every `schedules/*.bx` is a **BoxLang scheduler** : a plain class whose `configure()` builds tasks with BoxLang's own task DSL. There is no ColdBox in it and nothing to extend:

```javascript
// schedules/Nightly.bx
class {

	function configure() {
		task( "cleanup" )
			.everyDayAt( "00:00" )
			.call( () => run( "clean up old tickets" ) )
			.withNoOverlaps()
	}

}
```

The build copies each file into the app as `schedules/<Name>.bx`, lists them in `this.schedulers` of the [generated base `Application`](/next/conventions/application-bx/index.html), and BoxLang starts them with the app and stops them with it. They run while the app is served (`bxAgents serve`).
> **Note**
>
> A scheduler is for the developer. For prompts that the people who use the agent make for themselves, by asking it, see [routines](/next/conventions/routines/index.html).
> **Tip**
>
> `bxAgents add schedule` writes one for you: say when it runs, what to tell the agent, and which agent. See [`add`](/next/cli-reference/index.html#add-schedule).

## What you get without writing an `extends`

The build adds `extends="bxagents.Scheduler"` to any scheduler class that names no parent of its own. That class is copied into the app (`app/bxagents/Scheduler.bx`, reached as `app.bxagents.Scheduler` through the template's `/app` mapping; `bxagents.Scheduler` is the name you write and the build points it there) and gives your scheduler these methods:

|             Method              |                                                                 What it does                                                                  |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `task( name )`                  | BoxLang's task builder: `.every()`, `.everyDayAt()`, `.onWeekdays()`, `.cron()` (six fields), `.withNoOverlaps()`, `.call()` ...              |
| `run( input, params, options )` | Sends a message to the **default agent** , the root agent your `Agent.yml` or `Agent.bx` defines. Takes the agent's own `run()` arguments.    |
| `agent( name )`                 | Any agent in the project tree by the `name` its own definition declares, root or subagent at any depth. With no name it is the default agent. |
| `defaultAgent()`                | The root agent.                                                                                                                               |
| `getInstance( dsl )`            | WireBox's `getInstance()`, for anything else the app registered.                                                                              |
| `controller()`                  | The running ColdBox controller.                                                                                                               |

```javascript
// schedules/Digest.bx
class {

	function configure() {
		task( "weekly-digest" )
			.everyWeekOn( 1, "08:00" )
			.call( () => agent( "ResearchBot" ).run( "summarize this week's findings" ) )
	}

}
```

Everything is reached when a task fires, not when `configure()` runs, so a scheduler can be configured before ColdBox has finished starting.

If a class names a parent already (`class extends="my.BaseScheduler" {`), the build leaves it alone. Make your parent extend `bxagents.Scheduler` to keep the methods above.

## When it runs

Say it with the task's own methods. Each of these was served on BoxLang 1.19.0 and waited on until it fired:

```javascript
.every( 15, "minutes" )          // from when the app starts, then every 15 minutes
.everyHour()  .everyHourAt( 15 ) // every hour, or at :15
.everyDayAt( "09:00" )           // every day at 09:00
.onWeekdays( "08:30" )           // Monday to Friday; .onWeekends( "10:00" ) for the other two
.everyWeekOn( 1, "09:00" )       // 1 is Monday
.everyMonthOn( 1, "09:00" )
.onFirstBusinessDayOfTheMonth( "09:00" )
```

Times are `HH:mm` in the scheduler's timezone. Also available: `.startOn()`, `.endOn()`, `.when()`, `.withNoOverlaps()`, `.onSuccess()`, `.onFailure()` and timezones.

## Cron

`.cron( "..." )` needs **six fields**, with the second first:

```javascript
.cron( "0 */15 * * * *" )       // every 15 minutes
.cron( "0 0 9 * * 1-5" )        // 09:00:00 on weekdays
.cron( "0 30 8 * * MON-FRI" )   // 08:30:00 on weekdays
```

Lists (`1,3,5`), ranges (`1-5`), steps (`*/5`), month names (`JAN`) and day names (`MON`) work.
> **A five-field cron does not fire on BoxLang 1.19.0**
>
> BoxLang's documentation says `.cron()` takes five fields, and its parser accepts them, but a task written as `.cron( "* * * * *" )`, `.cron( "*/2 * * * *" )` or `.cron( "30 14 * * *" )` never ran in a served app or in a bare `boxlang schedule` run (minutes of waiting, no error). The same schedule as six fields, as `.every()` or as `.everyDayAt()`, ran on time. A five-field expression ticks once a minute and BoxLang then requires the second to be 0; in a probe the tick landed just before the minute, so the test failed every time. Treat it as a BoxLang bug: write six fields, or one of the methods above. `bxAgents add schedule` does this for you, and writes a typed five-field expression with a leading `0`.

## Retrieving an agent

Every agent in the project's tree is registered in the generated `config/WireBox.bx` under its own declared `name`. `agent( "ResearchBot" )` resolves it, and `run( ... )` is the root agent. Because `name` is also a WireBox binding key it must be **unique across the whole project** - `build` fails validation if two agents share one. See [subagents/](/next/conventions/subagents/index.html#retrieving-an-agent-from-schedules).

```yaml
# subagents/researcher/Agent.yml
name: ResearchBot
model: openai/gpt-5
```

## Validation

`build` checks, because each would otherwise only fail when the app starts:

* the file name becomes the class name (`schedules.<Name>`), so it must be letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. `my-job.bx` is refused; `MyJob.bx` is fine;
* two files that would make the same scheduler class are refused: rename one;
* a scheduler that extends `coldbox.system.web.tasks.ColdBoxScheduler` is refused, with what to change;
* a file in `schedules/` that is not a `.bx` file is ignored, with a warning so a schedule that quietly stopped running is visible.

A syntax error or a wrong agent name in the body surfaces when the app starts (`serve`), like any other BoxLang class.
> **ColdBox's scheduler is a separate thing**
>
> Chat-platform [gateways](/next/conventions/gateways/index.html) register their polling tasks with ColdBox's own app scheduler. That is untouched, and a project's `schedules/` never go through it.

markdown:
# Scheduling Background Work

There are two ways to make an agent do something on a clock, for two different people.

|            |      Scheduler (`schedules/*.bx`)      | Routine ([the last lesson](/next/course/routines-and-reports/index.html)) |
|------------|----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Made by    | You, the developer, in a file          | Anyone who uses the agent, by asking it                                   |
| Lives      | In the project, shipped with the agent | In the chat database, per person                                          |
| Runs as    | The app, with no person behind it      | The person who made it                                                    |
| Changed by | Editing the file and rebuilding        | Asking, while the app runs                                                |
| When       | BoxLang's task methods (this lesson)   | A 5-field cron or `every 30m`, read in the routine's time zone            |

Reach for a scheduler for what the *agent's owner* wants to happen whatever anyone says (a nightly clean-up, a digest
to a fixed audience). Reach for a routine for what one *person* wants ("every weekday at 9, check my orders").

Every `schedules/*.bx` is a **BoxLang scheduler** : a plain class whose `configure()`
builds tasks. There is no ColdBox in it and nothing to extend - the build adds the
base class that gives it `task()`, `run()` and `agent()`.

```javascript
// schedules/Nightly.bx
class {

	function configure() {
		task( "nightly" )
			.everyDayAt( "00:00" )
			.call( () => run( "cleanup" ) )
			.withNoOverlaps()
	}

}
```

BoxLang's task methods say when: `.every( 15, "minutes" )`, `.everyDayAt( "09:00" )`,
`.onWeekdays( "08:30" )`, `.everyWeekOn( 1, "09:00" )`, `.startOn()`/`.endOn()`, `.when()`,
`.withNoOverlaps()`, lifecycle hooks, timezones. `.cron()` works with **six** fields
(second first); a five-field one does not fire on BoxLang 1.19.0, see
[schedules/](/next/conventions/schedules/index.html#cron).

## Retrieving your agent

`run( ... )` sends a message to the **default agent** , the root agent your
`Agent.yml` defines. `agent( "TheAgentName" )` gets any other agent in the tree by the
`name` its definition declares (see [Composing Subagents](/next/course/11-composing-subagents/index.html)):

```javascript
task( "weekly-digest" )
	.everyWeekOn( 1, "08:00" )
	.call( () => agent( "ResearchBot" ).run( "summarize this week's findings" ) )
```

## Many schedulers

Each file is its own scheduler, so group tasks however you like: one file per job, or
related tasks together. BoxLang starts them with the app and stops them with it, so they
run while the app is served.

## Validation

`build` checks that each file name is a valid class name (`MyJob.bx`, not `my-job.bx`),
that a scheduler does not extend ColdBox's scheduler any more, and warns about a file in
`schedules/` that is not a `.bx` file. The body is real code: a syntax error or a bad
agent name surfaces when the app starts (`serve`), not at `build`.

## Try it

Acme wants a digest every weekday morning. Write the scheduler. (`bxAgents add schedule` writes the same shape from
`--when` and `--prompt`; its phrases have spaces, so with the 1.19.0 launcher it is easier to write the file.) It
asks the `researcher` subagent from [Composing Subagents](/next/course/11-composing-subagents/index.html) a question; `agent( "researcher" )`
finds it by the `name` its definition declares:

```javascript
class {

	function configure() {
		task( "morning-digest" )
			.onWeekdays( "08:30" )
			.call( () => agent( "researcher" ).run( "refund" ) )
			.withNoOverlaps()
	}

}
```

Build, and ask `inspect` what the project would schedule. `inspect` reads the source, so nothing has to run:

```bash
cd ~/bxagents-course/acme-support
bxAgents build
bxAgents inspect --section=schedule
```

```text
Build succeeded: <anything>/acme-support/.build/app
...
  schedules/Digest.bx  morning-digest  onWeekdays( "08:30" )  researcher
```

The task runs while the app is served (`bxAgents serve`), at 08:30 on weekdays, and the course does not wait for a clock.
A five-field cron in `.cron()` does not fire on BoxLang 1.19.0, so use the task methods or six fields
(`0 30 8 * * MON-FRI`), as [schedules/](/next/conventions/schedules/index.html#cron) explains. Routines have no such trap: they
store a five-field cron and the app's own one-minute heartbeat reads it.

## Checkpoint

`acme-support/schedules/Digest.bx` exists. `kit/resume.sh 16-scheduling-background-work` restores it; rebuild after.

Full reference: [schedules/](/next/conventions/schedules/index.html).

title: Secrets the Agent May Use
body: Secrets the Agent May Use Acme's orders system wants an API key. Where does it go? Not in Agent.yml or a tool (they are committed and packaged), and not in a chat message (it would sit in a transcript). The vault is the place for secrets that people hand to a running agent: sealed in the agent's database, used by a tool or an MCP server at the moment it needs one, and never shown to the model. What you will build A secret sealed in the vault with one allowed host, a tool that uses it without ever returning it, and the audit list that records the use. About 20 minutes. Vault, .env or Agent.yml ? Where For Changes by .env and environment variables Deploy-time settings and the model provider's key ( OPENAI_API_KEY ) Redeploying or restarting Agent.yml Only the name of a variable or secret ( ${env.NAME}`, `${vault.NAME} ), never a value Rebuilding The vault Secrets people give a running agent: they change, differ per person, and should not need a redeploy A person, while the agent runs There are two scopes. A user secret belongs to one person (their name as the server knows them) and nobody else can see or use it. An agent secret is shared by everyone who talks to the agent, and an admin manages it. Asking for a name finds the person's own first, then the agent's; a run with no person behind it (a scheduler) finds the agent's only. 1. Turn it on and look at it empty A vault: block gives the agent two tools ( vault_list , names only, and vault_request , which asks a person to add a secret) and makes the runtime scrub every vault value out of tool results before the model sees them. Add it at the end of Agent.yml and rebuild: vault: {} cd ~/bxagents-course/acme-support bxAgents build bxAgents vault status Build succeeded: <anything>/acme-support/.build/app Secrets: 0 Key: none yet (made when the first secret is saved) Database: <anything>/chat.db 2. Add a secret A value is never a flag and never typed in a chat message . From a terminal vault add asks for it in a hidden prompt; in a script it reads a pipe with --stdin . A secret can list the --hosts it may be sent to, and is refused anywhere else: printf 'demo-secret-value' | bxAgents vault add --name=ORDERS_TOKEN --description=Orders-API --hosts=orders.acme.test --stdin bxAgents vault list Saved agent secret [ORDERS_TOKEN]. It is sealed and cannot be shown again. NAME<anything>SCOPE<anything>OWNER<anything>HOSTS<anything>LAST USED<anything>ABOUT ORDERS_TOKEN<anything>agent<anything>orders.acme.test<anything>never<anything>Orders-API Each value is sealed with AES-256-GCM, and the sealed value is tied to its row, so copying it onto another row does not open it. The key is made the first time a secret is saved, in a file beside the database. Read the warning vault status prints now: bxAgents vault status Secrets: 1 Key: a key file next to the database Database: <anything>/chat.db The key file sits beside the data it protects: anyone who copies the data folder gets both. Set BXAGENTS_VAULT_KEY to a key you keep elsewhere (`bxAgents vault key` makes one). For a real deployment set BXAGENTS_VAULT_KEY where the agent runs and keep a copy somewhere safe. If the key is lost the secrets cannot be recovered , and BxAgents never makes a new key while secrets exist. 3. Use it from a tool A tool asks the vault for a value by name, passing its own arguments (which carry the run, so a person's own secret is found before the agent's) and the host the value is about to go to. This tool only reports that the key is set and how long it is. It never returns the key, and if it did, the scrubbing would take it out: class { @AITool( "Check that the orders API key is set, without showing it." ) function ordersApiKey() { var key = vault( "ORDERS_TOKEN", arguments, "orders.acme.test" ) return { set : true, length : len( key ) } } } Rebuild, and ask the scripted model, which has a rule for the word vault . # Secrets the Agent May Use

Acme's orders system wants an API key. Where does it go? Not in `Agent.yml` or a tool (they are committed and
packaged), and not in a chat message (it would sit in a transcript). The **vault** is the place for secrets that
people hand to a *running* agent: sealed in the agent's database, used by a tool or an MCP server at the moment it
needs one, and never shown to the model.
> **What you will build**
>
> A secret sealed in the vault with one allowed host, a tool that uses it without ever returning it, and the audit
> list that records the use. About 20 minutes.

## Vault, `.env` or `Agent.yml`?

|                Where                 |                                                 For                                                 |           Changes by           |
|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **`.env` and environment variables** | Deploy-time settings and the model provider's key (`OPENAI_API_KEY`)                                | Redeploying or restarting      |
| **`Agent.yml`**                      | Only the *name* of a variable or secret (``${env.NAME}`, `${vault.NAME}``), never a value           | Rebuilding                     |
| **The vault**                        | Secrets people give a running agent: they change, differ per person, and should not need a redeploy | A person, while the agent runs |

There are two scopes. A **user** secret belongs to one person (their name as the server knows them) and nobody else
can see or use it. An **agent** secret is shared by everyone who talks to the agent, and an admin manages it. Asking
for a name finds the person's own first, then the agent's; a run with no person behind it (a scheduler) finds the
agent's only.

## 1. Turn it on and look at it empty

A `vault:` block gives the agent two tools (`vault_list`, names only, and `vault_request`, which asks a person to add
a secret) and makes the runtime scrub every vault value out of tool results before the model sees them. Add it at the
end of `Agent.yml` and rebuild:

```yaml

vault: {}
```

```bash
cd ~/bxagents-course/acme-support
bxAgents build
bxAgents vault status
```

```text
Build succeeded: <anything>/acme-support/.build/app
Secrets:  0
Key:      none yet (made when the first secret is saved)
Database: <anything>/chat.db
```

## 2. Add a secret

A value is **never a flag and never typed in a chat message** . From a terminal `vault add` asks for it in a hidden
prompt; in a script it reads a pipe with `--stdin`. A secret can list the `--hosts` it may be sent to, and is refused
anywhere else:

```bash
printf 'demo-secret-value' | bxAgents vault add --name=ORDERS_TOKEN --description=Orders-API --hosts=orders.acme.test --stdin
bxAgents vault list
```

```text
Saved agent secret [ORDERS_TOKEN]. It is sealed and cannot be shown again.
NAME<anything>SCOPE<anything>OWNER<anything>HOSTS<anything>LAST USED<anything>ABOUT
ORDERS_TOKEN<anything>agent<anything>orders.acme.test<anything>never<anything>Orders-API
```

Each value is sealed with AES-256-GCM, and the sealed value is tied to its row, so copying it onto another row does not
open it. The key is made the first time a secret is saved, in a file beside the database. Read the warning
`vault status` prints now:

```bash
bxAgents vault status
```

```text
Secrets:  1
Key:      a key file next to the database
Database: <anything>/chat.db

The key file sits beside the data it protects: anyone who copies the data folder gets both.
Set BXAGENTS_VAULT_KEY to a key you keep elsewhere (`bxAgents vault key` makes one).
```

For a real deployment set `BXAGENTS_VAULT_KEY` where the agent runs and keep a copy somewhere safe. **If the key is
lost the secrets cannot be recovered**, and BxAgents never makes a new key while secrets exist.

## 3. Use it from a tool

A tool asks the vault for a value by name, passing its own `arguments` (which carry the run, so a person's own secret
is found before the agent's) and the host the value is about to go to. This tool only reports that the key is set and
how long it is. It never returns the key, and if it did, the scrubbing would take it out:

```javascript
class {

	@AITool( "Check that the orders API key is set, without showing it." )
	function ordersApiKey() {
		var key = vault( "ORDERS_TOKEN", arguments, "orders.acme.test" )
		return { set : true, length : len( key ) }
	}

}
```

Rebuild, and ask the scripted model, which has a rule for the word `vault`. Then read the audit list: every add,
change, removal and use, with who, from where and which host, and never a value:

```bash
bxAgents build
bxAgents invoke --message=vault
bxAgents vault audit
```

```text
Build succeeded: <anything>/acme-support/.build/app
The key check says: {set:true,length:17}
WHEN<anything>ACTION<anything>NAME<anything>SCOPE<anything>WHO<anything>VIA<anything>RESULT
<anything>use<anything>ORDERS_TOKEN<anything>agent<anything>tool<anything>ok
<anything>add<anything>ORDERS_TOKEN<anything>agent<anything>cli<anything>ok
```

The same secret could sit in an MCP server's header: write `token: ${vault.ORDERS_TOKEN}` in an `mcpServers` entry
of `Agent.yml`. It is resolved when the app starts, never at build time, so the value is not in the project, the build
or a package. Only the agent's secrets can be used there, because the app starts once for everyone.

## 4. The Vault page

In the web app the **Vault** page lists the secrets you can use, adds one into a hidden password field (sent once, the
field cleared) and, for an admin, shows the key's status and the same activity list. The terminal chat has `/vault`
for the same.

![The Vault page in the web app: secrets by name, purpose and hosts, and the activity list](/next/assets/webui/webui-vault.png)

## Limits worth knowing

* A static key or token only. OAuth sign-in and token refresh are not in the vault (the [connectors](/next/course/17-hosting-mcp-servers/index.html) use their own sealed sign-ins, stored the same way).
* A secret used in `Agent.yml` is read when the app starts: change it and restart.
* Protect the door as well as the safe: on an open server anyone who can reach the page is the admin, which is why [Who Is Allowed](/next/course/users-roles-and-tokens/index.html) comes first.

## Checkpoint

`Agent.yml` ends with `vault: {}` and `tools/OrdersApi.bx` exists. The secret itself is in your data home, sealed.
`kit/resume.sh the-vault` restores the project files; rebuild after.

Full reference: [the vault](/next/conventions/vault/index.html) and [`vault`](/next/cli-reference/index.html#vault).

Next: [Each Person's Own Settings](/next/course/layered-settings/index.html)

skills/ Each immediate subfolder of skills/ that contains a SKILL.md file is one skill, following the Claude Agent Skills convention: YAML frontmatter ( name , description ) followed by a body of freeform instructions. skills/ └── greeting/ └── SKILL.md --- name: greeting description: How to greet people warmly. --- Always greet the user warmly and use their name if known. Tip bxAgents add skill creates skills//SKILL.md with the frontmatter and a body to fill in. See add . The Registry page of the web app lists every skill with its level and opens its SKILL.md in a reader. /skills NAME and bxAgents skills show NAME do the same in the terminal. Naming The skill's name is its frontmatter name: if present; otherwise it falls back to the folder name ( greeting/ with no frontmatter name would be discovered as greeting anyway, but an explicit name: always wins even if it differs from the folder). Two skills resolving to the same name fail validation with a duplicate-name error. A folder without a SKILL.md inside it is not discovered as a skill at all - it's simply ignored (useful for scratch subfolders, assets kept alongside a skill under a different structure, etc., as long as they don't sit directly under skills/ themselves without a SKILL.md ). The three levels An agent's skill list is made from three levels, and a fourth that bxAgents brings itself. The first two are built into the app; the third is written by the agent while it runs. flowchart TB GL["Global skills folder
managed by a skills tool (npx, CommandBox)"] subgraph project["Your project"] direction TB INS[".agents/skills/
1. Installed
links to the global folder, or installed copies"] SHIP["skills/
2. Ships with the agent
written by you"] end subgraph app["The built app: skills/"] direction TB A1["copies of the installed skills
listed in .installed.json"] A2["copies of your skills"] end subgraph home["The data home: skills/"] DH["3. The agent's own
written by the agent with skill_save"] end LIST(["The agent's skill list
loaded by name when a task needs one"]) GL -. "symbolic link" .-> INS INS -->|build| A1 SHIP -->|build| A2 A1 --> LIST A2 --> LIST DH -->|"at start, and the moment it is saved"| LIST Level Where Written by origin in /skills 1. Installed .agents/skills/ in the project. A skills tool links a skill from its global folder into it, or bxAgents skills install copies one there. It stays out of source control and is restored at build time A skills tool or the registry installed 2. Ships with the agent skills/ in the project, and the skills extensions carry You project 3. The agent's own skills/ in the data home The agent, with its skill_save tool agent bxAgents' own skills/ inside the bxAgents module: how to build, operate and chat with an agent bxAgents bxagents The rules between the levels: Yours wins over installed. A skill in skills/ and an installed one with the same name or folder: the one in skills/ is used. The agent never replaces the first two. skill_save refuses the name of an installed skill or one that ships with the agent. It can save over a skill it wrote itself, to improve it. bxAgents' own come last. A skill of yours with the same name as one of the six that bxAgents ships wins, and skill_save cannot take their names. They are available on request like every skill: only a name and a description are in the context until the model asks for one. skills.builtin: false in Agent.yml leaves them out. A link is followed. The app gets a copy of what the link points at, so a deployed app does not depend on the global folder. The app tells levels 1 and 2 apart by skills/.installed.json , which the build writes beside the skills. /skills and GET /skills use it to show each skill's level. Level 3 is described in data and volumes : approval of each save, the limits, and the skills setting in Agent.yml . Skills from the registry Skills from skills.boxlang.io are installed with bxAgents skills install , not copied by hand. They go in .agents/skills/ (bx-ai's own default folder), out of source control; .agents/skills.lock.json is committed and build restores from it. Both folders go into the build, and a skill in skills/ with the same name wins. A global skills tool can link its skills into .agents/skills/ instead; a link is followed and the app gets a copy. See skills . How it's wired at runtime skills/ is copied verbatim into the generated app (same wipe-then-write, dotfile-excluding copy as tools/ ; a skill folder that is a symbolic link is followed and copied). The app's skills/ folder holds the project's own skills and the installed ones together. bx-ai reads its skills folder once, when the runtime starts, which is before an app's settings are applied. So the generated agent factory adds the app's skills/ folder to bx-ai's list of global skills itself, before any agent is built, and then the extensions' skills and the skills the agent saved in its data home. Every agent is given that one list, so the same skills are listed by GET /skills , the Registry page and /skills , and loaded by the agent's skill tool. It works the same for serve , for chat and for a packaged app, since all of them build agents from the same factory. The generated app also writes { "skillsDirectory": "/app/skills" } to config/bxai-settings.json (not config/Coldbox.bx , because ColdBox's moduleSettings does not reach bx-ai, a BoxLang module). Info bx-ai's own default skillsDirectory is /.agents/skills , a different path than BxAgents' skills/ convention. You never need to set it. Skills installed under your project's .agents/skills/ are copied into the app's skills/ at build time.

The agent's own | `skills/` in the [data home](/next/conventions/data/index.html#skills-the-agent-saves) | The agent, with its `skill_save` tool | `agent` | | bxAgents' own | `skills/` inside the bxAgents module: how to build, operate and chat with an agent | bxAgents | `bxagents` | The rules between the levels: * **Yours wins over installed.** A skill in `skills/` and an installed one with the same name or folder: the one in `skills/` is used. * **The agent never replaces the first two.** `skill_save` refuses the name of an installed skill or one that ships with the agent. It can save over a skill it wrote itself, to improve it. * **bxAgents' own come last.** A skill of yours with the same name as one of the six that bxAgents ships wins, and `skill_save` cannot take their names. They are available on request like every skill: only a name and a description are in the context until the model asks for one. `skills.builtin: false` in `Agent.yml` leaves them out. * **A link is followed.** The app gets a copy of what the link points at, so a deployed app does not depend on the global folder. * **The app tells levels 1 and 2 apart** by `skills/.installed.json`, which the build writes beside the skills. `/skills` and `GET /skills` use it to show each skill's level. Level 3 is described in [data and volumes](/next/conventions/data/index.html#skills-the-agent-saves): approval of each save, the limits, and the `skills` setting in `Agent.yml`. ## Skills from the registry Skills from skills.boxlang.io are installed with `bxAgents skills install `, not copied by hand. They go in `.agents/skills/` (bx-ai's own default folder), out of source control; `.agents/skills.lock.json` is committed and `build` restores from it. Both folders go into the build, and a skill in `skills/` with the same name wins. A global skills tool can link its skills into `.agents/skills/` instead; a link is followed and the app gets a copy. See [`skills`](/next/cli-reference/index.html#skills). ## How it's wired at runtime `skills/` is copied verbatim into the generated app (same wipe-then-write, dotfile-excluding copy as [`tools/`](/next/conventions/tools/index.html); a skill folder that is a symbolic link is followed and copied). The app's `skills/` folder holds the project's own skills and the installed ones together. bx-ai reads its skills folder once, when the runtime starts, which is before an app's settings are applied. So the generated agent factory adds the app's `skills/` folder to bx-ai's list of global skills itself, before any agent is built, and then the extensions' skills and the skills the agent saved in its data home. Every agent is given that one list, so the same skills are listed by `GET /skills`, the Registry page and `/skills`, and loaded by the agent's skill tool. It works the same for `serve`, for `chat` and for a packaged app, since all of them build agents from the same factory. The generated app also writes `{ "skillsDirectory": "/app/skills" }` to `config/bxai-settings.json` (not `config/Coldbox.bx`, because ColdBox's `moduleSettings` does not reach bx-ai, a BoxLang module). > **Info** > > bx-ai's own default `skillsDirectory` is `/.agents/skills`, a different path than BxAgents' `skills/` convention. You never need to set it. Skills installed under your project's `.agents/skills/` are copied into the app's `skills/` at build time.

# Slash commands

Type `/` in the terminal chat (a menu you move through with the arrow keys, see [the terminal UI](/next/guides/terminal-ui/index.html)) or the [web chat](/next/conventions/web-ui/index.html#slash-commands) to see the commands (on the web page the lightning button opens the same menu, and an extension's command carries the extension's name). Each one is written once, as a small class that answers with data, and every surface draws that answer its own way. In [chat platforms](/next/conventions/gateways/index.html#commands-in-a-gateway) type the command as a message; the default prefix is `/` and a gateway can change it.

**Where** is `T` terminal, `W` web page, `G` chat platforms. A command marked `G` still needs to be in the gateway's `allow` list; the default list is `help`, `info`, `tools`, `model`, `ping`, `notes` and `remember`.

![/sessions after naming and forking a conversation](/next/assets/tui/chat-sessions.png)

*`/name`, `/fork` and `/sessions` in a real chat.*

## Conversations

|                   Command                    | Where |                                                                                                                                               Does                                                                                                                                               |                               Example                               |
|----------------------------------------------|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `/new`                                       | T W G | Start a new conversation. The old one stays in the list                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `/new`                                                              |
| `/sessions`                                  | T W G | List your recent conversations, numbered                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `/sessions`                                                         |
| `/resume [number or id]`                     | T W G | Go back to one and show what was said. No argument: the most recent                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `/resume 2`                                                         |
| `/name <name>`                               | T W   | Name this conversation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `/name Quarterly plan`                                              |
| `/fork [name]`                               | T W   | Copy this conversation, messages and all, and carry on in the copy                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `/fork Other approach`                                              |
| `/clear`                                     | T W G | Forget this conversation's messages, keep the conversation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `/clear`                                                            |
| `/settings [name] [value\|reset] [--global]` | T     | Terminal only. Open the settings panel, or show, change or reset one setting. A name that is not one of the chat's own is a setting of the agent's `Agent.yml` and applies the next time the agent starts. A change is saved for this agent in its data home, or for every agent with `--global` | `/settings header compact`, `/settings model ollama/qwen3 --global` |
| `/cls`                                       | T     | Terminal only. Clear the screen above the message box and the scrollback. The conversation stays, while `/clear` forgets its messages. Ctrl+L does the same                                                                                                                                      | `/cls`                                                              |
| `/compact`                                   | T W G | Replace older messages with a summary and keep the latest few (`keepRecent`). The agent's own model writes the summary, unless its memory names a summary model                                                                                                                                  | `/compact`                                                          |
| `/export [file] [--format=md\|html]`         | T W   | Save the conversation. The file name decides the format unless `--format` says                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `/export plan.html`                                                 |
| `/exit` (alias `/quit`)                      | T     | Leave the chat                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `/exit`                                                             |

On a gateway, `/new`, `/clear`, `/compact`, `/sessions` and `/resume` are off until the gateway sets `commands.conversation: true`.

## Know what is going on

|                                    Command                                     | Where |                                                                                                                  Does                                                                                                                   |           Example            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| `/help`                                                                        | T W G | List the commands you can run here                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `/help`                      |
| `/info`                                                                        | T W G | Agent, model, conversation, message count, notes and database, and each setting that came from one of your own `Agent.yml` files with the file                                                                                          | `/info`                      |
| `/tools`                                                                       | T W G | List the agent's tools                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `/tools`                     |
| `/volumes`                                                                     | T W G | List the folders the agent may use, by name, mode and description. Never a folder on the machine                                                                                                                                        | `/volumes`                   |
| `/agent [name]`                                                                | T     | Terminal only. List the agent and its sub-agents, or switch to one and start a new conversation with it. Every agent keeps its own memory. The web page has the **Talk to** menu for this, and a gateway always talks to the main agent | `/agent researcher`          |
| `/skills`                                                                      | T W G | List the skills the agent can load, and its level: installed, project, bxagents or agent                                                                                                                                                | `/skills`                    |
| `/routines [all]`                                                              | T W   | List your [routines](/next/conventions/routines/index.html): schedule in words, status and next run (an admin adds `all`).                                                                                                              | `/routines`                  |
| `/routine <name> [run\|pause\|resume\|delete confirm\|reports\|report <file>]` | T W   | Show one routine, or act on it. `delete` needs `confirm`, and no command removes a report                                                                                                                                               | `/routine check-build pause` |
| `/context`                                                                     | T W   | How big the context is and what it is made of, and how many of the messages its memory keeps this conversation has (a warning near the limit). Worked out locally, no model call                                                        | `/context`                   |
| `/stats [days] [--by=model\|provider\|day\|user]`                              | T     | Tokens the model calls used. `/stats enable` turns usage recording on                                                                                                                                                                   | `/stats 7 --by=day`          |
| `/keys`                                                                        | T W   | Opens the shortcuts panel: which key does what, with the action name of each, narrowed by typing. `?` alone does the same                                                                                                               | `/keys`                      |

## Models

|      Command      | Where |                                                              Does                                                               |     Example     |
|-------------------|-------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| `/model`          | T W G | Show the model in use, its profile, context window and vision support                                                           | `/model`        |
| `/profile [name]` | T     | Pick a [profile](/next/conventions/models/index.html#profiles) from a list, or switch straight to one. The conversation is kept | `/profile fast` |
| `/default`        | T     | Go back to the app's default model                                                                                              | `/default`      |
| `/ping [profile]` | T W G | Test that the model answers, with one tiny question. Says how long it took, or why it did not                                   | `/ping fast`    |

Over `--connect` or `--server`, `/profile` can only switch among the profiles the server lists in [`agentApi.profiles`](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#agentapi).

## Notes

|                        Command                         | Where |                                                                                                                             Does                                                                                                                              |               Example               |
|--------------------------------------------------------|-------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `/remember <text>`                                     | T W G | Keep a note about you                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `/remember I prefer short answers`  |
| `/notes`                                               | T W G | Open the notes screen (terminal)                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `/notes`                            |
| `/connect`                                             | T W G | List the connectors and the services that ask you to sign in, and whether you are connected; `/connect NAME` connects one (a token goes in a hidden box on the terminal), `/connect NAME off` disconnects, `/connect NAME tools` lists and switches its tools | `/connect github`                   |
| `/logs [area] [--tail=N] [--level=warn] [--grep=text]` | T     | The agent's logs: which there are, or the last lines of one. Admin only; over `--connect` it takes an admin token. To follow one live, `bxAgents logs <area> --follow` or `--ui`                                                                              | `/logs gateways --level=warn`       |
| `/vault`                                               | T W G | Open the vault screen (terminal), or list the secret names. A value is never typed in a command                                                                                                                                                               | `/vault`                            |
| `/notes list`                                          | T W G | Print your notes and the agent's, with how full each is                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `/notes list`                       |
| `/notes add [agent] <text>`                            | T W G | Add a note about you, or with `agent` about the agent's work                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `/notes add agent Use metric units` |
| `/notes edit <id> <text>`                              | T W G | Change a note; the id is the short code in the list                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `/notes edit a3f New text`          |
| `/notes remove <id>`                                   | T W G | Remove a note. Removing the agent's needs an `admin` token over `--connect`                                                                                                                                                                                   | `/notes remove a3f`                 |
| `/notes stats`                                         | T W G | Characters used against the limit, and the rough tokens they add                                                                                                                                                                                              | `/notes stats`                      |

## Your terminal

These act on your own machine or your own session, so they stay in the terminal (`/extensions` also works in the web page).

|             Command              | Where |                                        Does                                        |                 Example                  |
|----------------------------------|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `/extensions [name]`             | T W   | List the extensions the chat loads and what each added; with a name, one in detail | `/extensions`                            |
| `/reload`                        | T     | Load the extensions and their settings again. Admin only                           | `/reload`                                |
| `/prompt [style]`                | T     | Show or change the message box look for this chat                                  | `/prompt box`, `/prompt top +git -clock` |
| `/copy`                          | T     | Copy the last answer to the clipboard (OSC 52, honoured by most terminals)         | `/copy`                                  |
| `/record [file]`, `/record stop` | T     | Record the screen as a `.cast` file                                                | `/record demo.cast`                      |

## Add your own

`/extensions` and `/reload` come with the [extension](/next/conventions/extensions/index.html) support. An extension adds commands such as `/deploy` or `/roll 2d6` to the chat, and [a first extension](/next/guides/first-extension/index.html) walks through one. The commands over HTTP are `GET /__bxagents/commands` and `POST /__bxagents/command`, see [Run control](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#run-control).

title: subagents/
body:
subagents/ subagents/ holds nested agents, each an ordinary BxAgents project of its own - an Agent.yml + instructions.md (and optionally its own tools/ , skills/ , etc.). A subagent's tools/ belong to it alone, and its tools: list is its own; neither is inherited from or shared with its parent: my-agent/ ├── Agent.yml # subAgents: [ researcher ] ├── instructions.md └── subagents/ └── researcher/ ├── Agent.yml └── instructions.md A subagent is wired to its parent by name, declared in the parent's Agent.yml subAgents list - the subagents/ FOLDER name to wire at build time: # Agent.yml name: my-agent model: openai/gpt-5 subAgents: - researcher The same list in a class-based Agent.bx (the advanced form ) goes in configure() , distinct from super.init() 's own subAgents argument (which takes already-built AiAgent instances, not names). A project can mix the two forms: a YAML root with a class subagent, or the reverse. At build time, bx-ai's addSubAgent() wraps each built subagent instance as a callable tool on the parent automatically - there's no separate tool-wrapping step to write yourself. Tip bxAgents add subagent creates the folder, asks the same questions as new for its model and tools, and adds it to the parent's subAgents . --parent= nests it under another subagent. See add . In the web app the Talk to menu lists the main agent and each sub-agent; the next message goes to the one you pick, and each keeps its own memory. In the terminal it is /agent . The Agent page draws the whole tree. Flat namespace, sibling references Every subagent - no matter how deeply another subagent's own config references it - lives directly under the root project's subagents/ folder. A subagent's own declared subAgents names reference sibling entries in that same root-level folder, not a folder nested under itself. This keeps the discovery/validation model simple: one flat directed graph over subagents/ 's immediate subfolders, rather than a tree that could nest arbitrarily deep on disk. Flat on disk, a graph in config, built bottom-up - the three views of the same project: flowchart LR subgraph disk["ON DISK - always flat, one level under the ROOT project"] direction TB R1["subagents/A/"] R2["subagents/B/"] R3["subagents/C/"] end subgraph declared["DECLARED - each definition's own subAgents list"] direction TB GA["A"] --> GB["B"] --> GC["C"] end subgraph built["BUILT - leaf-first, in GeneratedAgentFactory.bx"] direction TB O1["1. build C"] --> O2["2. build B
with the built C"] --> O3["3. build A
with the built B"] end disk -.->|"names resolve
against siblings"| declared declared -.->|"a parent needs its
children already built"| built style disk fill:#eef2f7,stroke:#5a6570 style declared fill:#e7f1ff,stroke:#004085 style built fill:#eaf6ec,stroke:#155724 A cycle in the declared graph ( A -> B -> A ) is rejected at validation, before any of this is generated; a diamond (two parents sharing one descendant) is fine. Build order Subagents are built leaf-first (bottom-up): if A declares subAgents: ["B"] and B declares subAgents: ["C"] , the generated GeneratedAgentFactory.bx builds C , then B (passing in the built C instance), then A (passing in the built B instance) - never the other way around, since a parent's aiAgent() call needs its children's already-built instances. Validation A subagent name in subAgents that doesn't correspond to a real subagents/{name}/ folder (holding an Agent.yml or Agent.bx ) fails validation with a clear "references unknown subagent [...]" error - this applies to every node's subAgents list, including the root project's own definition, not just nested subagents. Circular references ( A → B → A ) are rejected at validation time, with the full cycle path reported (e.g. A -> B -> A ), before any code generation happens. A "diamond" shape - two subagents both depending on the same shared descendant - is not a cycle and builds fine; only genuine cycles are rejected. A missing Agent.yml / Agent.bx inside a discovered subagents/* folder is reported as its own validation error, and so is a folder holding both ( BxAgents.AmbiguousAgentDefinition ) - a folder holds one definition. Every node's own DECLARED name (root + every subagent's own definition) must be unique across the whole project - see below. Retrieving an agent from schedules/ Two different names are in play, and they're not interchangeable: The folder name under subagents/ ( researcher above) is what subAgents: [ "..." ] references - it's purely a build-time wiring concern. The subagent's own declared name (its agent definition's name field, e.g. "ResearchBot" ) is what you retrieve it by at runtime - every agent in the tree (root + every subagent) is registered in config/WireBox.bx under this name, so a schedules/ scheduler reaches it with agent( "ResearchBot" ) (and any other WireBox-aware code with a plain getInstance( "ResearchBot" ) ). These two names can differ, and often will - the folder name is an implementation detail, the declared name is the one that matters everywhere else (prompts, WireBox retrieval). Because it's now also a WireBox binding key, build fails validation if two agents in the tree - however deeply nested - end up with the same declared name , including two that both leave it unset and silently share the "BxAi" default.

against siblings"| declared declared -.->|"a parent needs its
children already built"| built style disk fill:#eef2f7,stroke:#5a6570 style declared fill:#e7f1ff,stroke:#004085 style built fill:#eaf6ec,stroke:#155724 ``` A cycle in the declared graph (`A -> B -> A`) is rejected at validation, before any of this is generated; a diamond (two parents sharing one descendant) is fine. ## Build order Subagents are built **leaf-first** (bottom-up): if `A` declares `subAgents: ["B"]` and `B` declares `subAgents: ["C"]`, the generated `GeneratedAgentFactory.bx` builds `C`, then `B` (passing in the built `C` instance), then `A` (passing in the built `B` instance) - never the other way around, since a parent's `aiAgent()` call needs its children's already-built instances. ## Validation * A subagent name in `subAgents` that doesn't correspond to a real `subagents/{name}/` folder (holding an `Agent.yml` or `Agent.bx`) fails validation with a clear "references unknown subagent \[...\]" error - this applies to **every** node's `subAgents` list, including the root project's own definition, not just nested subagents. * **Circular references** (`A` → `B` → `A`) are rejected at validation time, with the full cycle path reported (e.g. `A -> B -> A`), before any code generation happens. * A "diamond" shape - two subagents both depending on the same shared descendant - is **not** a cycle and builds fine; only genuine cycles are rejected. * A missing `Agent.yml`/`Agent.bx` inside a discovered `subagents/*` folder is reported as its own validation error, and so is a folder holding both (`BxAgents.AmbiguousAgentDefinition`) - a folder holds one definition. * Every node's own DECLARED `name` (root + every subagent's own definition) must be unique across the whole project - see below. ## Retrieving an agent from `schedules/` Two different names are in play, and they're not interchangeable: * The **folder name** under `subagents/` (`researcher` above) is what `subAgents: [ "..." ]` references - it's purely a build-time wiring concern. * The subagent's own **declared `name`** (its agent definition's `name` field, e.g. `"ResearchBot"`) is what you retrieve it by at runtime - every agent in the tree (root + every subagent) is registered in `config/WireBox.bx` under this name, so a [`schedules/`](/next/conventions/schedules/index.html) scheduler reaches it with `agent( "ResearchBot" )` (and any other WireBox-aware code with a plain `getInstance( "ResearchBot" )`). These two names can differ, and often will - the folder name is an implementation detail, the declared `name` is the one that matters everywhere else (prompts, WireBox retrieval). Because it's now also a WireBox binding key, `build` fails validation if two agents in the tree - however deeply nested - end up with the same declared `name`, including two that both leave it unset and silently share the `"BxAi"` default.
